The confirmed, full results in Germany's Saxony-Anhalt regional election are likely to be a major political headache for Chancellor Friedrich Merz, whose centre-right Christian Democrats (CDU) party have governed the eastern state for more than 20 years.

Sunday evening’s exit poll showing the far-right, pro-Russian, Alternative for Germany (AfD) potentially gaining 44.5 per cent of the vote is beyond the 40 per cent recent opinion polls had been showing and well in excess of the 20.8 per cent the party secured in 2021. Mr Merz's CDU fell to 18.5 per cent in the exit poll from 37.1 per cent in 2021. The CDU currently leads a coalition with the centre-left Social Democrats (SPD) and the free-market Free Democrats (FDP).

About 1.7 million people were eligible to vote in the east-central state of 2.1 million residents. Participation was at a record high of 76.5 pert cent

The AfD had been looking to secure an absolute majority of above 50 per cent, to ensure they could try and implement their own radical agenda.

So what happens now?

1. The AfD seize power

If the AfD were to take control of the regional parliament, they would be the first far-right party to have power in either a regional or the national parliament since the Second World War. If this were to happen, what is known in Germany as the "firewall" – where parties create coalitions to keep far-right parties from power – would be breached for the first time.

open image in gallery Ulrich Siegmund, top candidate in the Saxony-Anhalt state election for the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) ( AFP/Getty )

The AfD has been clear about what it would do if it were to take power. It seeks to restrict immigration, quit the Euro and restore ties with Russia as most of Europe rallies around Ukraine.

Based on the party’s “Vision 2026” election manifesto, victory in Saxony-Anhalt could invite sweeping reforms around state policy on migration, education, culture and the family.

Under Germany's federal system, state governments sit in the upper house of parliament, the Bundesrat, and also have wide powers in education, domestic security and culture.

An AfD-led state would launch a crackdown on migration with a task force set up to coordinate quicker deportations.

The children of refugees would be placed in separate classes at school to prevent what the party claims are “stresses” on the other children from being around different cultures.

Meanwhile children with disabilities would no longer be taught in the same classroom as those without, instead, being sent to new schools.

Schools would also be banned from flying rainbow flags, and the government would exhaust “all legal avenues” to limit Islamic expression.

The party has claimed greater acceptance of what it offensively labels as"sexual deviations and non-reproductive lifestyles" has contributed to sinking birth rates and promises to aggressively promote "traditional" family structures consisting of a mother, father and children. An AfD government would see major changes to the school curriculum around a “patriotic cultural policy”, extended to raising the German national flag daily and singing the national anthem at school celebrations.

open image in gallery Alternative for Germany (AfD) co-leader Alice Weidel ( AFP/Getty )

It would also advocate for removing war refugee status for Ukrainians in Germany as long as the conflict remains concentrated in eastern Ukraine, arguing they should seek refuge in western Ukraine.

The current structure of the public broadcasting system would be dismantled and funding withdrawn for some cultural institutions.

In terms of domestic security in Saxony, the AfD in the state is assessed by Germany's domestic intelligence agency as a "far-right extremist" group, which would create concerns about the intelligence the AfD would be able to see if it was in charge of the regional parliament.

However, the AfD will likely need the support of another party, depending on how many smaller parties pass the five per cent threshold needed to get seats. In Saxony-Anhalt, all the parties except the small far-left BSW party have ruled out joining a coalition with the AfD.

If some smaller parties do not pass the threshold though, it would make the AfD's job easier as it would make the chance of a coalition against it less likely.

The party will talk to any sensible party with whom it can find common ground on policy positions, said AfD national co-leader Alice Weidel after the exit poll

2. The CDU pull together a coalition

The CDU has been hit hard, but may yet be able to pull together a "firewall coalition". That is what happened in the state of Thuringia in 2024, where the AfD gained more than 30 per cent of the vote, but not enough for an absolute majority.

However, American think tank the Brookings Institution believes this will be difficult. “The task of organizing a CDU-led governing majority faces almost insurmountable difficulties” it said in a recent briefing note, exacerbated by the CDU’s ruling out of any coalition with the far-left The Left party. The Left party has indicated it would be open to an arrangement formalising support for a CDU-led government over the AfD. But the CDU faces internal divisions over a possible alliance with the ideologically remote far-left.

open image in gallery German Chancellor and Christian Democratic Union (CDU) party leader Friedrich Merz ( Reuters )

Mr Merz said ahead of the election last Sunday that they would “assess the situation in light of the election results” and “do everything we can to prevent Saxony-Anhalt from falling into the hands of the radicals”.

State premier Sven Schulze congratulated the AfD in the wake of the exit poll and acknowledged the result showed it was the strongest party. If the AfD is unable to rule outright, it could trigger a protracted process of coalition building by mainstream parties who are determined to keep a party under investigation for right-wing extremism by Germany's domestic intelligence service out of power.

3. The German government takes a hit regardless

However the political wrangling in the wake of the Saxony result ends up, it is clear that the manner of the AfD's win is important for their national standing and a blow to Mr Merz's coalition government.

Nationwide, the AfD has swollen to become the most popular party, polling at 29 per cent, while Mr Merz has become the most unpopular chancellor since the founding of the Federal Republic, with 85 per cent of voters dissatisfied.

Lars Klingbeil, co-leader of Germany's centre-left SPD party and vice chancellor in Mr Merz's governing coalition, said after the exit poll that the result of the Saxony-Anhalt state election is a signal for Berlin politics. The result is ⁠a reason to reflect on the federal government’s policies, Mr Klingbeil told public ‌broadcaster ZDF. “And ​rest ‌assured, that ⁠is what ⁠we will ‌do.”

Mr Merz has already sought to create a harder line on immigration, in a move designed to try and stem the rise of the AfD. There will no doubt be a greater push from the AfD to try and move the needle on national policy, while their pro-Russia stance could be an issue when it comes to European support for Ukraine, given the nation has previously been accused of moving cautiously when it comes to handing Ukraine weapons to fight off Russia's invasion.

Mr Merz will face an increasing level of political pressure about his own job and government, something the AfD will be all too happy to try and press home in both future regional elections and the wider national polls.

The Trump administration has renewed its appeal to the Supreme Court to allow new restrictions on mail ballots ahead of the midterms after a federal judge issued a preliminary injunction.

U.S. District Court Judge Indira Talwani extended an order against the Postal Service enforcing President Donald Trump’s executive order for the November elections Friday.

The legal wrangling comes even as states start sending out mail ballots, leaving the administration little time to make big changes in mail ballot rules.

In the filing, Solicitor General John Sauer said: “Ballots have already begun to be mailed in North Carolina, and more States will begin the mailing process as the injunction remains in place — including Alabama on September 9 and at least five States the week of September 13.”

“Once those ballot envelopes enter the mailstream, there is no retrieving them. And while the injunction allows the Postal Service and the States to continue taking steps to ensure that their envelopes satisfy the Rule’s requirements ... each day the injunction is in place risks sowing confusion and chaos because the injunction makes those preparatory steps voluntary, rather than mandatory.”

The appeal marks the third time the administration has asked the high court to intervene. The high court has allowed the plan to move forward but not ruled on whether it is legal.

Trump has long sought to limit mail voting, even though he himself often uses that method to cast his own ballot ( AFP/Getty )

The battle could have major ramifications for this year’s elections, when control of Congress is at stake. Nearly one-third of voters in the U.S. cast mail ballots.

Democratic states and voting rights groups say the changes are unconstitutional.

Election officials contend there isn’t enough time to revise their systems to comply with the new Postal Service directives.

The Trump administration has framed the restrictions as commonsense changes that are within its power to regulate the mail.

“Simply put, the best way to address respondents’ fears about inability to comply with the Rule is to grant an immediate administrative stay of the order, followed by a full stay pending further review,” Sauer said. “That will remove the improper cloud of uncertainty that the district court has cast over the Rule, making clear to all involved that compliance with the Rule is not optional and must start without further delay.”

The filing added that eligibility for mail-in and absentee voting will continue to be governed by state law and state and local officials will determine who is eligible to use the method and which ballots are eligible to be counted. “The Postal Service will not play any role in determining voter eligibility, maintaining voter rolls, or counting ballots.”

Trump has long sought to limit mail voting, even though he himself often uses that method to cast his own ballot. He has falsely blamed mail balloting for his 2020 election loss to Democrat Joe Bden, spreading baseless claims of fraud. But so far, he has been unable to change the longstanding voting procedure.

George Russell admitted it is going to be “exceptionally challenging” to prevent Kimi Antonelli from beating him to the world championship after his rival produced a stunning fightback drive from 19th to win the Italian Grand Prix.

Antonelli became the first Italian to triumph at Monza’s Temple of Speed since Ludovico Scarfiotti stormed to victory 36 days after England last won the World Cup.

Sixty years on and hit with an engine penalty, Antonelli began Sunday’s contest virtually at the back. But the 20-year-old phenomenon capitalised on an explosive new power unit, a favourable strategy, and a demonstration of passing excellence, to see off a crestfallen Russell by passing him for the lead with just three laps left.

open image in gallery Antonelli celebrates winning on home soil (Bradley Collyer/PA) ( PA Wire )

No driver since Ulsterman John Watson won the 1983 United States Grand Prix at Long Beach has taken the chequered flag from further behind. It marks another piece of history for Antonelli who is firmly on course to become the youngest Formula One world champion.

For Russell, this was supposed to his year. This was supposed to be his Italian Grand Prix. He started the race 17 positions ahead of Antonelli.

However, he is now 66 points behind the Italian with just 10 scheduled rounds remaining. Russell has just two victories to Antonelli’s seven. The momentum is with Antonelli and, to add insult to injury, Russell was jeered on the podium by the partisan Italian crowd.

“It is definitely Kimi who is in control of it (the championship battle) and he is deserving to be in control,” said Russell. “I am not even thinking about a fight or a comeback.

open image in gallery Russell (left) was reeled in by Antonelli (Bradley Collyer/PA) ( PA Wire )

“It is going to be exceptionally challenging to overcome that gap. I am sort of accepting that is what it is. And I am going to try and enjoy it from here on in and win as many races as possible.”

Russell will have earmarked the 13th round of the season as his golden chance to eat into Antonelli’s title lead. But he will head for the inaugural Madrid race next weekend even further behind.

The writing appeared on the wall by only the second lap of the restart – after Charles Leclerc crashed out at 160mph – when Antonelli was already up to sixth. By lap 18, Antonelli was second and on Russell’s tail.

Russell and Antonelli traded position five times for the lead. The former remained in front only for a Virtual Safety Car to lean the fixture in his team-mate’s favour.

open image in gallery Antonelli is the first Italian to win at Monza since 1966 (Bradley Collyer/PA) ( PA Wire )

Antonelli was on the medium rubber – less durable than Russell’s hard tyres – before he was handed 25 laps on fresh mediums to catch and pass Russell.

Russell’s advantage after Antonelli stopped for new tyres stood at 14 seconds but with 10 laps to go, his margin had been trimmed to five seconds. He was looking increasingly vulnerable.

Antonelli looked to have blown his chance when he ran through the gravel at the Variante del Rettifilo as he attempted to wrest the lead off Russell on the 49th lap.

But Antonelli was immediately back on Russell’s gearbox and he made no mistake when he breezed past his wounded team-mate before crossing the line 3.8 seconds ahead.

The strategy appeared to favour Antonelli and Russell might have felt aggrieved with his Mercedes team.

But the magnanimous Brit explained: “The VSC came out at that perfect point for the drivers (behind) to pull the trigger and take the pit stop.

“I didn’t (consider pitting). I actually thought the guys behind me were going to stay out. I am sure the team were quite nervous on the pit-wall watching our battle and they were probably happy to send us out on different strategies.

“I was on the hard tyre and Kimi was on the medium, so if one of us was going to pit, it was going to be Kimi and that is why I was a little bit annoyed with the timing of the VSC because it would have been tough for those guys on the mediums to have competed with anyone on the hards, but it takes nothing away from Kimi’s drive.

“And obviously when you are racing in somebody else’s home country that (the boos) is to be expected. I smiled it off.”

The far-right Alternative für Deutschland (AfD) party is set for a historic regional election win in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt – in a blow for German chancellor Friedrich Merz.

Exit polls have placed the AfD party at 44.5 per cent, up ⁠from 20.8 per cent in 2021. Mr Merz's CDU fell to 18.5 per cent from 37.1 per cent in 2021, a setback in a state the conservatives have governed since 2002.

If the full results, expected on Monday, show that the AfD has secured a majority, the party could form its first regional government in what would be a seismic moment in post-war German history. However, given that most ‌parties have ⁠ruled out joining ⁠an AfD-led coalition, it will depend on which other parties pass the 5 per cent threshold needed to gain seats in the regional parliament and whether the CDU could form a majority coalition to block the AfD.

The party’s victory in the election for the state government represents a historic shift in German politics after years of cooperation between the other parties to keep the hard right out of power.

open image in gallery Supporters of far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) celebrate, after polls closed in the Saxony-Anhalt state elections, in Magdeburg, Germany ( Reuters )

The AfD seeks to restrict immigration, quit the Euro and restore ties with Russia as most of Europe rallies around Ukraine. Germany’s own intelligence service has designated the party as ‘extremist right wing’.

Ulrich Siegmund, lead candidate for the AfD in Saxony-Anhalt, hailed the projections, saying: “We have made history in this country”.

He said that he was open to work with partners following the exit poll results, adding: “We extend a hand to all democratic forces that wish to pursue better policies”. But also said that topics including migration and domestic security were non-negotiable.

This win is the biggest prize in the party's 13-year history, at a time of widespread discontent with an unpopular national government that has yet to persuade voters it can get the country's sluggish economy moving.

open image in gallery Ulrich Siegmund, top candidate in the Saxony-Anhalt state election for the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) ( AFP/Getty )

Victory for the AfD is also a symbolic blow to Mr Merz, whose centre-right party has led Saxony-Anhalt for 24 years.

The AfD national co-leaders, Alice Weidel and Tino Chrupalla, said this week that AfD "wants to implement the law of the land — for example with a view to illegal migration — and ensure that Germany remains worth living in."

open image in gallery Co-Chairwoman of the Bundestag AFD faction Alice Weidel, Ulrich Siegmund, lead candidate of the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) and Co-Chairman of the Bundestag AFD faction Tino Chrupalla celebrate a first exit poll win ( Getty )

They decried other parties' records and argued in a statement that an absolute majority for AfD is "almost the only chance to change course."

Following the poll results on Sunday, Ms Weidel said that the AfD had a clear government mandate and would talk to all parties.

"No matter the outcome of tomorrow's election, we have already made history," said its candidate for governor, Ulrich Siegmund at a final rally on Saturday evening.

"Because what we have started here in Saxony-Anhalt — that is currently sweeping across all of Germany — can no longer be stopped," he told the crowd in the state capital, Magdeburg.

open image in gallery Sven Schulze, Premier of Saxony-Anhalt and member of the German Christian Democratic Union (CDU) reacts to initial results in Saxony-Anhalt state elections following the closure of polling stations ( Getty )

The AfD plans to push schools and cultural institutions towards more traditional values, curb immigration and overhaul public broadcasting.

Mr Siegmund arrived to cast his vote in his hometown of Tangermuende on a blue Simson moped, greeted by throngs of excited fans, and ruled out coalition talks with other ​parties.

An AfD-led state would launch a crackdown on migration with a task force set up to coordinate quicker deportations.

The children of refugees would be placed in separate classes at school to prevent what the party claims are “stresses” on the other children from being around different cultures.

Meanwhile children with disabilities would no longer be taught in the same classroom as those without, instead being sent to special schools.

Schools would also be banned from flying rainbow flags, and the government would exhaust “all legal avenues” to limit Islamic expression.

News.title: Maitland-Niles’s last-gasp debut goal salvages Everton’s miserable week
News.content:
At the final whistle, the first song the stadium DJ played was Spirit of the Blues and how those relieved Evertonians lapped it up after a week of angst.

Their team had been on the precipice of a defeat that would have exacerbated all the frustrations that bubbled away following the chaotic conclusion to the transfer window. Indeed, it was 10 seconds over the allotted five minutes of added time when the ball fell to Ainsley Maitland-Niles.

It had been three years since the former Arsenal full-back had played in the Premier League – his last goal in England was on October 30, 2019, in an EFL Cup tie with Liverpool at Anfield that ended 5-5 – and he would not have joined Everton if their attempt to sign Kenny Tete from Fulham had not failed.

But here he was 30 yards from goal, with no need to break his stride as Manchester United’s backtracking defenders presented him with an invitation to shoot. So that’s what he did. With one perfectly timed swish of his right foot, an unlikely hero transformed the mood of a club.

News.title: Antonelli ends 60-year wait for home winner after starting 19th at Italian GP
News.content:
Kimi Antonelli showed why he appears to be Formula One’s champion-elect as he became the first Italian since Ludovico Scarfiotti 60 years ago to win his home race, despite starting 19th.

Antonelli, who elected to take a grid penalty at Monza for taking a new engine, spent the entire race hunting down Mercedes team-mate George Russell, finally passing the Briton on lap 50 of 53.

Antonelli benefited from an early red flag after Charles Leclerc smashed into the barriers at Parabolica on what was an awful day for Ferrari.

Antonelli also took advantage of a mid-race virtual safety car to switch tyres when Russell stayed out in the lead.

News.title: VAR a scourge on the Premier League as Forest denied by off-field meddling
News.content:
“I don’t know if it’s streetwise but he knows how to win,” Maresca said, who is in line to hand Fernández his debut against Coventry on Saturday. “When you want to compete or win, it’s much more important to have players that already know how to do that than players who have never done it in the past.

“Enzo is not the only one. This squad has many players who know how to win titles and how to compete and this is what we are looking for.

“I know Enzo quite well and I know what he can bring to the team. He is a winner, [has] a winner’s mentality and knows how to win [after] the World Cup, Club World Cup [success].

“I just said he is a winner and when you belong to the squad and another winning player arrives, they are always happy.

“I can promise you that in the last four or five days, four or five players from the squad were asking if was coming or not because they wanted him to be with us. It’s very important that he is with us.”

Maresca said he planned to use Fernandez predominantly as a No 6 or No 8 depending on the game. “I see Enzo as a six, a little bit more deep, or [an eight] a little higher arriving in the box,” he said.

News.title: Newcastle’s limitations exposed by Bournemouth before hosts fight back for draw
News.content:
A reality check is not necessarily a bad thing. There has been a lot of hype and excitement on Tyneside and a self-congratulating tone to their own end of summer appraisals.

But this was a reminder of the team’s limitations and the fact that only three of their eight summer signings started the game, with two more coming off the bench, underlined they are a work in progress.

In truth, that is fine. It is the start of September and the Premier League campaign is only three games old. They have a new manager and a new-look team. There has been a significant amount of change in a very short period of time.

It was not the easiest summer, and despite the insistence from senior figures at the club that they had always remained calm and methodical during their summer reset, there was a whiff of crisis only a few weeks ago.

When Eddie Howe quit as manager and Bruno Guimarães, the captain, forced his move to Arsenal at the start of August, Newcastle looked in disarray. So, to have started the season unbeaten from three games against Liverpool, Tottenham Hotspur and Bournemouth is encouraging.

It is also worth highlighting just how good the visitors were. In the first half Bournemouth were superb, rushing Newcastle, forcing mistakes and pouring forward in numbers. In Alex Scott, just as he was in their victory here last season, Bournemouth had the best player on the pitch.

That opens up another conversation. Newcastle played like this a lot at home in Howe’s final season in charge, especially in the second-half of the campaign, but tended to lose not draw the game.

On this occasion, they secured a decent point with a late equaliser thanks to substitute Ramsey, who looked good when he replaced the off-colour Lewis Miley.

Bournemouth will feel they should have held on. They had taken a deserved lead through Marcus Tavernier, who took advantage of a static and ball-watching Amar Dedić to bundle home from close range.

News.title: Relentless Springboks give All Blacks 15 minutes of hell to lead series
News.content:
There will be no repeat of the All Blacks historic Test series victory in South Africa 30 years ago, after the home side ruthlessly ensured they will lead 2-1 going into the concluding weekend.

And the manner in which the Springboks blew away their fierce rivals in the last 15 minutes made Rassie Eramus’s men overwhelming favourites to finish the job in America next Saturday.

However, there were passages of this brutal battle that suggested that Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry could still produce a finale worthy of the billing if New Zealand can learn the lessons from this brutal encounter at the FNB Stadium in Johannesburg.

There was a late Kiwi try to give the scoreboard a humdinger hue but Erasmus’s side were well deserving of their second victory in as many Saturdays over their fierce rivals, and credit to the South Africa coach for outwitting counterpart Dave Rennie without needing to change his starting XV just before the kick-off, like he did seven days before.

Amazing what one can do with a simple but chilling game plan. The old scoundrel knew that if he slowed it down and let his scrum walk round the All Blacks scrum that his backs would have the precious space.

Yet, however it might feel away from Springbok turf, New Zealand will still fancy their chances of levelling it, especially after matching their opponents’ haul of four tries. Their fly-half, Ruben Love, missed five simple-enough points and until that last quarter it was an even contest. Yet, as it tends to, South Africa’s physical intensity and their almighty scrum eventually prevailed.

News.title: Gasly takes shock Italian GP pole and denies Russell
News.content:
Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of and qualifying for the Monza Grand Prix.

Before the weekend’s racing, George Russell was, at least publicly, less than bullish about his chances in Italy.

He did, though, believe he would deliver a better showing than he had in recent weeks.

“I don’t know if we can say we’re favourites this weekend, but we probably have a greater opportunity than we’ve had in the last two races where it’s been less about the power unit and more about the chassis,” he said.

“It’s so close right now, that last tenth in qualifying can be the difference of a couple of positions, which can change the podium. Right now, I don’t know who is going to be the team to beat.”

Russell was almost a minute off winner Lando Norris of McLaren in Hungary, finishing seventh in his Mercedes. Two weeks ago, in the Netherlands, he took the last spot on the podium, with Norris winning again.

However, in the second practice session on Friday and FP3 today, Russell was quickest. He led his former colleague, Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton, who was second fastest.

Red Bull’s Max Verstappen hinted at a rare good weekend as he was third fastest, about a third of a second behind Russell.

Russell, of course, needs a win soon, or he is in danger of seeing the championship run away from him entirely, as Kimi Antonelli already leads him by 59 points in the world title chase.

Perhaps psychologically just as pressing is that erstwhile teammate Hamilton is tied with Russell on 183 points, in third because he has one victory compared to Russell’s two. Slipping down the rankings could knock his confidence.

Russell has not secured pole for the last four races, so a strong showing in qualifying might be the boost he needs ahead of Sunday’s race, while Norris is looking for a pole position hat-trick.

News.title: ‘It’s just a useless gimmick’: Telegraph readers react to Dyson’s latest gadget
News.content:
Would you spend over £400 on a toothbrush? Telegraph readers aren’t convinced.

The new Dyson CameraJet has just launched, retailing for £419.99, which brushes, flosses and mouth-washes in one, with the help of a camera.

After Rebecca Astill gave her verdict on the gadget, we asked Telegraph readers for their views and whether Dyson can convince them to trade in their old faithfuls.

They share the toothbrushes they swear by, from manual to electric models, and whether they see any reason to upgrade. Here’s what they had to say.

Why readers are unconvinced

The majority of readers seem unconvinced by the CameraJet, with John arguing that a toothbrush and a smartphone “sounds like two accidents waiting to happen. Squirted in the eye with mouthwash as you drop the phone down the toilet”.

“It’s just a useless gimmick,” argues reader Donald Mckie, a retired NHS dentist. “The average patient wouldn’t have a clue what they would be looking at in their mouth on a phone screen,” he adds.

“Dyson as a brand is an aspiration for many but I don’t know how this appliance would improve anyone’s oral health.”

In his view, “the tank for the mouthwash at 12.5ml is far too small, the industry average will be somewhere near 250-300ml” to last long enough and successfully dislodge sticky plaque.

He also questions the picture quality of the camera with water spray, saliva, lips, facial hair and toothpaste in the way. “People nowadays will expect pin sharp detail, which I doubt this will deliver.”

News.title: DiCaprio’s Amazonian warrior queen
News.content:
It was while she was in hiding after recovering from the sixth attempt on her life, that the activist Juma Xipaia got a call asking if she would agree to be the subject of a documentary. The first female chief of the Middle Xingu region of the Brazilian Amazon, Xipaia was well known in Brazil for her passionate attempts to protect her indigenous community from the effects of deforestation, illegal gold-mining and – in particular – the catastrophic environmental consequences of the $11 billion Belo Monte hydroelectric dam project, a wildly ambitious and destructive endeavour that has affected livelihoods, fish stocks, ecosystems and biodiversity, with legal challenges still ongoing today.

Thirty-four-year-old Xipaia’s outspoken resistance and exposure of corruption relating to the dam’s construction led to the threats on her life. The last attempt was by poisoning, via a food delivery company, which resulted in her being on a ventilator with 70 per cent organ failure. She was on the verge of death, when, she says, she had a dream that she was given a choice – to take the easy path of dying, or the difficult path of coming back, and because she’s a fighter, that’s the one she chose. And a week later she walked out of the hospital.

Leonardo DiCaprio described the activist as one of the most incredible people he’d ever met Credit : Lalo de Almeida/Folhapress, FSP

Like many activists representing indigenous communities she walked a tightrope between protecting the interests and traditions of her people, and not being perceived as standing in the way of progress in terms of the economic development that benefits Brazil as a whole, a paradox that was defined when President Lula da Silva regained power in 2023, and brought Xipaia into government.

Richard Ladkani, a film director who has made vibrant environmental documentaries such as The Ivory Game (about poaching) and Sea of Shadows (marine activists), was the man who called her. It was 2019, when Brazil was still under the brutal rule of Jair Bolsonaro and destruction of the Amazon was at its peak – an area of rainforest the size of Belgium was burned during his presidency, and thousands of illegal goldmines flourished, contaminating the forest, polluting the river with mercury (mercury is used to bind gold) and bringing crime and disruption to previously pristine areas.

Film-maker Richard Ladkani in the Brazilian Amazon Credit : Courtesy of Malaika Pictures

“All summer long we had seen these dramatic apocalyptic images,” says Ladkani. “And I was posing for photos at the premiere of Sea of Shadows, with [executive producers] Leo DiCaprio and Jane Goodall, when Leo leaned over and whispered, ‘So Richard, what’s next?’

“And I said, 'We've got to do something about the Amazon.’”

DiCaprio came onboard as producer, and Goodall as an ambassador. Ladkani knew he had to find a powerful central figure to provide human and emotional context, someone who would be the voice of the Amazon. He drew up a list of possible candidates, until the Brazilian journalist Eliane Brum told him “do not make a decision until you have spoken to Juma Xipaia – when she speaks, the world listens. She can silence a whole room with her energy.”

‘For a long time I had been seen as a soldier, an army of one’

Right now, in a small restaurant in New York, Xipaia is not really in the mood to talk. It is February, and it’s snowing, and Ladkani, Xipaia and her husband, Hugo Loss, are here to publicise the resulting documentary, Yanuni – which took six years to make – at a screening attended by UN representatives and Brazilian diplomats. The recent news about Trump’s exploits in Venezuela has shaken them all and, more specifically, Juma has had a bad experience with American food which doesn’t really agree with her. She is a little reticent at first, but soon opens up with the help of an interpreter, and explains to me what it meant to be a cacique (chief), and how she was selected.

Indigenous leader Juma Xipaia and her husband Hugo Loss in the city of Aracaju, Brazil Credit : Lalo de Almeida/Folhapress, FSP

“I never chose to be a cacique,” she says, “but I couldn’t stay quiet in the face of exploitation of my people – there was violence, and women being harassed and raped.” She is referring to the collateral damage that importing thousands of workers to build a dam inevitably brings. “Usually the role of cacique is given to the oldest male in the community – my dad and my uncles and my brother were all caciques, but the elders knew that they could trust me never to negotiate our rights with corporations or politicians, never to compromise. For a long time I had been seen as a soldier, an army of one. I accepted the position for two years, with the goal of strengthening on our territories and bringing sovereignty to our people.”

Xipaia was born in 1991 and had an idyllic childhood, she says, growing up in Tucumã, a small indigenous community along the Iriri River, about 250 miles west of the city of Altamira. They lived in wooden houses and ate fruit and nuts from the forest and fish from the river, and in 2006 she moved to Altamira for her education. But threats were encroaching her community, with land opened up for mining and farming, and in 2011, a licence was granted to construct the Belo Monte Dam, to stop up parts of the Xingu River, one of the most species-rich areas of the Amazon.

Aged just 21, Xipaia spoke out against the dam at a public hearing, but despite lawsuits, protest from indigenous people and large sections of society, construction went ahead. Xipaia attended law school in Altamira and studied plans put forward by Norte Energia, the company that built Belo Monte, helping to expose corruption that was going on within. In 2015, at the age of 24, she became a cacique, the first female leader of her people. Other communities had been bought off by Norte Energia with gifts of stoves, fridges, TVs.

In November 2019, she led a protest of angry Brazilian landowners and farmers to disrupt the Amazon: Center of the World international conference in Altamira. But by now she had become a target, and by the time Ladkani called her she had survived six attempts on her life, including her car being rammed with children in the back, and a threat to kidnap her son. She went into hiding for a year and she didn’t want to talk to anyone.

“She thought, the only way I’m going to survive is if I stop talking, because when I talk, people want to kill me,” Ladkani says. But she was finally convinced to take a call from him, and from the first moment, he says, he knew he had found the voice for his film. “Her poetry is the thing that stands out – the way she can describe emotions and feelings and put things into context, I felt it was unique. And when she told me the story of how she almost died because of the poisoning, I was in tears.

“I told her I wanted her to be the voice in the film and also offered her the role of producer. Because I knew nothing of indigenous life and I needed her to lead the way.”

An aerial view of the Belo Monte hydroelectric dam in Altamira Credit : CARLOS FABAL

It was a struggle from the word go. Xipaia was not happy about a translator being involved because of security reasons; she couldn’t trust anyone. So Ladkani, who is Austrian, took intensive lessons in Portuguese and within six months was fluent. “It was a key thing to show that I meant business and took her concerns very seriously,” he tells me.

The security budget for the film was huge, they needed the best, most experienced people: safe houses, secure drivers. And the arrangements had to extend for a year after filming was completed – a total of seven years. “Leo was extremely important here because he raised the first third of the budget, and this encouraged other philanthropists to be part of it.”

Filming began in 2020. There was no script and Ladkani didn’t know what he was going to get from it, just that he needed to tell the story of the pillaging of the Amazon via Xipaia’s voice.

And in the end it was a wild ride: it started with Xipaia leading protests against Bolsonaro, but after Lula was elected in 2023, he established a Ministry for Indigenous Rights, of which Xipaia was made state secretary, implementing a series of bills for the protection of the forest and employing lawyers, biologists and engineers to combat the destruction of the Amazon.

Juma Xipata and Leonardo DiCaprio at the Yanuni Premiere during the 2025 Tribeca Festival in New York City. Credit : John Nacion/Getty Images for Tribeca Festival

The film documents her move from her village to set up home in Brasilia with her son; getting together with her husband Hugo Loss, head of special operations for Ibama (the Brazilian Institute of Renewable and Natural Resources), an elite outfit conducting raids on illegal mines; and the birth of their first child, who was called Yanuni.

It was a lengthy, exciting journey, an improvisation which resulted in thousands of hours of film. “I just had to go with the unpredictable. The strength of any documentary is when unforeseen things happen, because a twist in direction is the greatest thing of any film structure.

“And we had that multiple times. I had chosen a woman to be the voice of the Amazon and two years later she became the second most powerful woman in the Indigenous Ministry – I get goosebumps now at the sheer luck. That was the first twist, and then Hugo enters her life, who happens to be this charismatic soldier of an elite force who would take me to the frontline of the Amazon resistance, and then Juma becomes pregnant and gives birth to Yanuni. Holy s**t. If I had written that as a script, everyone would have thrown it out as complete fiction.”

‘I said, how dangerous is it? And he said, “Well, the risk of you dying is 50 per cent”’

Leo DiCaprio was a producer on the film (rather than his usual role of executive producer), which meant he was far more involved. “He not only provided the money, but he gave me meaningful support throughout the production,” says Ladkani. In November 2021 DiCaprio attended Cop 26 in Glasgow, where he met Xipaia for the first time. “That meeting was spectacular – Leo posted a picture of the two of them together and said that she was one of the most incredible people he’d ever met.” The resulting attention helped to protect Xipaia, because a public profile is to some extent a safeguard. “There she is next to DiCaprio, so she’s not just a voiceless indigenous person from somewhere in the Amazon.”

There were many technical challenges. Because of security, Ladkani couldn’t film in the normal way, with lighting and a crew. “I had a second cinematographer, a brilliant guy from Brazil, called Fábio Nascimento, and I took him with me when I could – but that was only 30 per cent of the time. The rest I shot alone. I downsized my gear and basically shot the film with a DSLR, like a photo camera, so I looked like a tourist. To an outsider, I was just a white gringo taking pictures.” Xipaia had a hidden microphone beneath her shirt. If Ladkani was ever confronted, he claimed to be a YouTuber.

“Security demanded that we shot the film incognito, and that became its strength, because I was embedded within the family to the extent that they stopped noticing me,” says Ladkani.

An illegal gold-mining ship destroyed by Ibama in the Brazilian Amazon – it is dangerous work, with agents risking serious injury and even their lives Credit : Courtesy of Malaika Pictures

Hugo Loss’s job involved protecting indigenous communities and flying over the forest and rivers of the Amazon routing out illegal goldmines, dredgers and excavators. His small team lands, arrests the miners and sets fire to all the expensive equipment, which is too bulky to confiscate. In the film we see massive plumes of thick black smoke rising above the forest. Penalties for environmental crime are insubstantial, but, says Loss, “It’s not for President Lula to change those things, it’s Congress, and it’s hard to change the law. But destroying the equipment is a real deterrent, because the machines are expensive, so it’s a risky investment.”

An illegal gold mine in the Brazilian Amazon Credit : Courtesy of Malaika Pictures

Loss and Xipaia met when her village was attacked in 2020 by illegal goldminers; she was in Altamira, a two-day boat ride away. She put out a cry for help on social media and Loss, who was also in Altamira, saw it and responded right away. He picked Xipaia up in a helicopter and asked her to take him to the exact location of the miners’ dredger. The attackers spotted them and ran, but Ibama were able to seize their boat and secure the area. “He saved her village and her people and her parents from an immediate attack and they fell in love and have been together ever since,” says Ladkani.

“I’m usually very shy about these things but from the first time I saw her in the helicopter I couldn’t stop thinking about her,” admits Loss. “Three months later I was doing an Ibama operation on land to remove some illegal loggers and I saw a hawk’s nest and I took a picture of it and sent it to her,” says Loss.

“It’s the bird whose feather I wear in my headdress,” interrupts Xipaia, shyly. She admits that she had first met Loss before the helicopter ride, at a meeting, but he was leaving as she arrived. “He shook my hand and I made eye contact with him and something told me – I can’t really explain what – that he was going to be my husband.”

Loss holds a Master’s degree in social anthropology from the University of Brasília and is one of Ibama’s most experienced field agents, yet he spent a good part of his career sidelined by Bolsonaro, who had no interest in protecting the environment. In February 2023, under Lula, he was appointed Ibama’s coordinator of enforcement.

Loss has taken part in hundreds of operations. His job is a dangerous one. We watch him flying helicopters over swathes of forest to spot mines, or patrolling the rivers looking for dredgers. Recently one of his team was killed in an ambush, another got burns over 60 per cent of his body.

Hugo Loss, Xipaia’s husband, on a mission to destroy illegal mining equipment for Ibama, Brazil’s government enforcement agency

Ladkani asked to accompany Loss on a raid. “Hugo told me, it's too dangerous, the risk of you dying is too high. It’s a small team, and you would be taking the place of a soldier on the helicopter so we would be down one security man, which means our job is much harder, and by the way, if we get into a gun fight, we are not your bodyguards, we are there to finish a job. You would have to save yourself.

“I said, how dangerous is it? And he said, ‘Well, the risk of you dying is 50 per cent.’ I laughed – and then I realised he wasn’t joking.

Film-maker Richard Ladkani in the Brazilian Amazon Credit : Courtesy of Malaika Pictures

“Of course I had to think about that – I have a wife and two daughters. My wife and I discussed it. She grew up in a war zone in Beirut, so she understands threats, and how you can mitigate risks as well. She is also the producer of this film. We have had a long journey together – making conflict zone films like Sea of Shadows and The Ivory Game was no joke. But this one felt like a different level because of the 50 per cent quote.” He smiles.”‘I did hostile-environment training and we augmented the security to a degree where I felt it wasn’t 50 per cent any more.”

An illegal airbase in the Brazilian Amazon being destroyed Credit : Courtesy of Malaika Pictures

So Ladkani joined the team, and the resulting episode is terrifying: they are patrolling the river when they find a huge illegal dredger, used for gold mining. They board the dredger, its crew of illegal miners are put in a small boat and dispatched, and Loss’s team set fire to it. Attempting to get away, they realise their boat is still attached to the dredger by a chain, and they have only moments before an oxygen tank below the deck of the dredger explodes. Loss has to shoot the chain, but he has to hit it while it is taut, or the bullet would glance off. “The oxygen tank is steel and if it had exploded we would have been killed by the fragments if we were within 100 metres of that boat – and we were six metres away. It was Hugo who shot the chain – it took 50 shots at least. When Juma saw that footage she broke down and sobbed,” says Ladkani.

Do you like your job? I ask Loss.

He smiles. “Yes I do.”

Back in the 1970s, when two major roads were originally carved into the Amazon rainforest, of which 60 per cent is in Brazil, it opened it up for settlers to devastating effects – the population of the Brazilian Amazon quadrupled and millions of acres of trees were cut down for timber or land clearance and farming, and the rivers became polluted. Thousands of garimpeiros (prospectors) arrived, bringing disease, destruction and violence.

Indigenous people from the Mura tribe in a deforested area inside the Amazon rainforest near Humaita, Amazonas State, Brazil Credit : Ueslei Marcelino/REUTERS

Despite the protected reserves created by Lula during his first tenure (2003 to 2011), when Bolsonaro took over, he vowed that he would not demarcate a single millimetre of Indigenous land.

There was reason to be hopeful when Lula was re-elected in 2023, especially when he created the Ministry for Indigenous People. But it was an uphill struggle, and Xipaia left the post of State Secretary after about two years, and retired to her territory, where she still is. “She realised that it would be years, if not decades, before change could happen and she felt that her power was with activism from the front lines rather than being in an office in the city,” says Ladkani. “And what really hurt was her children having to grow up in the city and not having the connection to nature that she had.”

Smoke from illegal fires lit by farmers rises in Manaquiri, Amazonas state Credit : MICHAEL DANTAS

There has been a lot of progress, Juma says, compared to the Bolsonaro years “when it was genocide”. “It is hard to quantify all the changes because even though there was a change in the administration, it is important to understand that the government structure is very colonialist, no matter who is in power, and everything takes time. I entered the ministry when it was just being born.

“It was hard working in an office every day and not spending time with my children, and my son Tuppak [eight] told me that he wanted to go back to the forest, he was having a hard time at school in the city. I did not want to rob my son of that kind of childhood – being in the territory and getting his knowledge from the forest.”

I ask Loss and Xipaia if, with the way things are now, they are more inclined to hope or despair. “Most of the time I don’t think about the future,” says Loss. “I just focus on doing my work, one operation at a time.”

A wildfire consumes land deforested by cattle farmers near Novo Progresso, Para state, Brazil Credit : MICHAEL DANTAS/AFP via Getty Images

Xipaia thinks. “It depends where I am. When I’m in the forest with my family, there is immense fulfilment which is hard to explain; it gives me the hope and energy to keep wanting to protect it, and I want the whole world to get to know it.

“When I walk through the forest and harvest food there with my family and my people, it reminds me of what my ancestors were doing. The innocence of children, the idea of clean water, food without toxins – this gives me hope.”

“I don’t feel despair,” says Ladkani. “I feel like we’re in a war. There are plenty of good people fighting back, and that gives me hope. And there are lives on the line that we need to care about, which is the indigenous people, who are the frontline of our defence. They are defending nature for us so we need to make sure that they are heard and seen and respected. And we hope that the film puts a human face to that.

“We can’t pretend that destroying the biggest ecosystem on the planet is OK. If we lose the Amazon, we all lose.”

Yanuni will be released later this year

Sports.title: Ex-Liverpool and Newcastle ace vindicated after wife refused to move for transfer
Sports.content:
Ex-Liverpool and Newcastle ace vindicated after wife refused to move for transfer

Former Liverpool goalkeeper Loris Karius decided to move to German side Schalke after his exit from Newcastle United despite the wishes of his wife Diletta Leotta

View 3 Images Loris Karius has enjoyed a crowning moment following his suprising move to Schalke in 2025 (Image: Ulrik Pedersen/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Former Liverpool and Newcastle goalkeeper Loris Karius put in a man of the match peformance as Schalke pulled off a remarkable draw against Bayern Munich in the Bundesliga. The German side were promoted to the top-flight but lost their opening match against Augsburg before producing a stunning upset against the champions.

‌



Karius kept a clean sheet in the goalless draw and earned plaudits from his opposite number, Manuel Neuer, in a jubilant moment for Die Knappen. The 33-year-old was central to ending two Bayern records as the stalemate marked the first time in 59 competitive matches that Bayern failed to score and the first time in 67 Bundesliga matchdays that Bayern will not finish the weekend at the top of the table.

‌



"Loris Karius was very good and definitely the right choice for Man of the Match. We had three big chances that he kept out," Neuer admitted. "That was definitely key to us not winning this game."

‌



Karius was happy to credit his team-mates for their efforts, suggesting that he didn't have much to do despite his notable impact. "It was great for me," he said.

Gary Neville issues on-air apology as VAR statement released on Arsenal goal vs Chelsea READ MORE :

FIFA boss Gianni Infantino to stand for re-election despite failed coup and calls to leave READ MORE :

"I only had to shout to keep going, move up, drop back. Real credit to the guys for what they did.

"They kept so much away and made things so incredibly hard for Bayern.

‌



"The guys really worked hard until they couldn't go anymore. Everyone today can be proud of their performance."

View 3 Images Bayern Munich boss Vincent Kompany congratulates Loris Karius (Image: UWE KRAFT / AFP via Getty Images)

Karius joined Schalke as a free agent 18 months ago, joining the side as back up to Justin Heekeren. The German goalkeeper, who started his senior career with Mainz, joined the club in January 2025 in controversial circumstances.

‌



Having gone without a club following the expiry of his contract at Newcastle, Karius opted to move to Germany against the wishes of his life Diletta Leotta. The television presenter had hoped that her husband would join her in Italy where she has been a part of Serie A broadcasting.

Leotta was said to have struggled to understand Karius' move to Germany as he attempts to kickstart his career once again. His efforts against Bayern might have been some vindication.

View 3 Images Diletta Leotta and her husband Loris Karius walk the carpet at the 2025 FIFA Club World Cup Draw (Image: Leonardo Fernandez - FIFA)

‌



Speaking following his move in 2025, Karius admitted that Leotta was full behind it regardless of her feelings. "Of course she was hoping a little for Italy," Karius told reporters.

"I explained it to her. She wishes me the best in my career and said she is fully behind it.

"Milan is not far away. We can find ways to solve it. She has a lot to do too, so we will both be commuting back and forth a bit.

Article continues below

"If your partner is also in the public eye, it's clear that something will be reported. But I never actively pushed myself into it. For me, the sport was always the priority."

Sports.title: Maitland-Niles screamer breaks Man Utd hearts and earns Everton draw - 5 talking points
Sports.content:
Maitland-Niles screamer breaks Man Utd hearts and earns Everton draw - 5 talking points

EVERTON 2-2 MAN UTD: The Red Devils looked set to be on the way to three huge points at Hill Dickinson Stadium only for debutant Ainsley Maitland-Niles to secure a share of the spoils

View 3 Images Ainsley Maitland-Niles enjoyed a dream debut for Everton (Image: Getty Images)

Ainsley Maitland-Niles scored an absolute stunner to steal a point against Manchester United on his Everton debut.

‌



Bryan Mbeumo struck the opener moments into the second half following a barnstorming run and lethal finish. Tyrique George thought he had ensured a share of the points, only for Benjamin Sesko to nod home late on to seemingly steal victory.

‌



The drama was not over there as Maitland-Niles climbws off the bench to fire home a late cracker to seal a draw for Everton and David Moyes.

‌



Here are all of the talking points from Hill Dickinson Stadium:

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Chances wasted

After his treble against Ipswich last weekend, Bruno Fernandes unsurprisingly went the closest to opening the scoring on Merseyside, having struck the bar with a powerful volley. Matheus Cunha then had a great opportunity but blazed over.

‌



Thierno Barry should have given the home side the lead before the break as he got on the end of a teasing cross but lifted his header over. While chances came and went, fans did not have to wait long for the goals to come.

Mbeumo blasts Man Utd ahead

While United were left frustrated in the first half, it didn't take long into the second for Michael Carrick's men to hit the front. After picking up the ball on the right flank, he cut inside and charged past a number of challenges before firing a lethal drive into the bottom corner.

It represented his second goal of the season, as well as his first-ever career goal against Everton.

‌



View 3 Images Bryan Mbeumo celebrates his second goal of the season (Image: Getty Images)

George answers Moyes call

There is one sure-fire way to get the crowd back on side and that's a stunning goal. And that's exactly what George provided.

The former Chelsea youngster received the ball on the right and thumped a brilliant effort into the roof of the net. Having been beaten at his near post, Senne Lammens might have felt he could have done better.

‌



But George will not care one jot. The forward has been backed to become an emergency striker by boss Moyes and given his finish, he might not be far wrong.

Sesko the super sub

Coming into this season, there was hope that Benjamin Sesko would begin to stamp his authority over the side. That has not quite come to fruition quite yet.

Ahead of the trip to Merseyside, Sesko had yet to find the net this season. But he was in the right place at the right time to nod home for the Red Devils.

‌



And while he might have a feeling of disappointment right now that his goal was not the winner, it might just be the tonic he needs to ignite his season and, hopefully, his Manchester United career.

View 3 Images Benjamin Sesko thought he was the matchwinner at Everton (Image: Getty Images)

Maitland-Niles announces himself

The arrival of Ainsley Maitland-Niles might not have been the inspirational signing that Everton fans wanted on deadline day despite the dire need for a right-back. Some might suggest that they're feeling a little bit silly now.

Article continues below

The former Arsenal man fired home an absolutely stunning effort deep into stoppage time to seal a point. And that might just be what Everton and boss Moyes need to lift the gloom on Merseyside.

Sports.title: FIFA boss Gianni Infantino to stand for re-election despite failed coup and calls to leave
Sports.content:
FIFA boss Gianni Infantino to stand for re-election despite failed coup and calls to leave

Gianni Infantino has been under the cosh after his World Cup sale attempts but despite calls for the FIFA president to go, he's look to remain in his post

View 2 Images Despite calls to stand down, Gianni Infantino is looking to remain as FIFA boss (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Gianni Infantino will stand for re-election as FIFA president even after the World Cup scandal. Infantino has been under intense pressure to quit after his scrapped plan to sell stakes in the World Cup caused a massive backlash.

‌



UEFA have called on him to stand down and other nations across the world are also applying pressure on Infantino before the next round of elections in March.

‌



FIFA president Infantino said in April that he would stand again for re-election in 2027 - and that has been reiterated by world football’s governing body.

‌



FIFA said in a statement: “The Fifa president announced in April that he will stand for re-election in 2027,” read a Fifa statement. Of course, nothing has changed. Mr Infantino will be standing for re-election.”

That will not please UEFA and their member associations like the English FA who were hoping that Infantino would quit and a new candidate would step forward.

‌



Infantino’s position has even come under pressure internally after the plans were revealed to sell stakes which caused a high backlash. Infantino is in Poland for the women’s under-20s World Cup and was carrying on as business as usual this weekend.

On Saturday, Infantino arrived in Katowice and said on Sky: “There will be a lot to say" but "it's not today.”

View 2 Images UEFA have put huge pressure on the FIFA boss to stand down (Image: Masashi Hara, Getty Images)

‌



It is the first time Fifa has said he will run for a fourth term since the aborted sell-off plan was announced following the summer's World Cup. FIFA rules say a president can serve a maximum of four terms and if he is successful then he will serve until 2031. The deadline for candidates to lodge their nominations is on November 18.

FIFA this week accused UEFA of a “smear campaign against it and its leadership”, in a challenge to litigation over Infantino's plan.

Last week UEFA filed legal papers in the US requesting disclosure of evidence and documents from Fifa, warning it could lodge a criminal complaint in Switzerland.

Sports.title: 'I found out I wasn't in Man Utd squad on social media after deadline day move was blocked'
Sports.content:
'I found out I wasn't in Man Utd squad on social media after deadline day move was blocked'

Manchester United left one former star in the dark when he reportedly discovered his squad snub via social media

View 2 Images Ex-Man United stopper Sergio Romero was denied an exit from the club after learning he'd failed to make the squad on social media (Image: Getty )

Former Manchester United goalkeeper Sergio Romero was devastated to discover he'd been left out of the squad via social media in 2020. The former Argentina stopper moved to Old Trafford from Sampdoria in 2015 but endured six uneventful years with the English giants.

‌



Having been a regular at club and country level during the earlier stages of his career, Romero was originally brought in as backup for David de Gea. However, he was rarely used by United in higher-priority competitions and made just 61 appearances for the club.

‌



His United tenure hit a new low ahead of the 2020/21 season when he was left out of their Premier League squad. This came after ESPN reported he was priced out of a move away, with Everton refusing to pay the £10million exit fee United allegedly insisted upon.

‌



Having made 17 appearances in all competitions for United the previous campaign, Romero found himself entirely sidelined in the 2020/21 campaign. The South American failed to record a single outing for the club and was finally allowed to leave on a free in 2021 when he joined Venezia.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Romero, 39, won the Europa League, FA Cup and EFL Cup during his stint at Old Trafford. However, his squad snub left a bitter taste in the mouth of those closest to the goalkeeper.

‌



Man Utd stars' feelings on two transfers emerge as Luke Shaw verdict given READ MORE :

Unai Emery makes telling Alejandro Garnacho comment as ex-Man Utd star slumps to new low READ MORE :

The matter was made worse by speculation Romero had learnt of that development through social media. And the rejection led to his partner going public herself to dig the club out over their tactics.

"He helped the team reach four finals/semi-finals and then was left on the bench only to lose them all," wrote Romero's wife, Eliana, on Instagram at the time. "It is time for them to return the opportunity and let him go. RESPECT FOR ONCE!!!

View 2 Images Romero kept 39 clean sheets in 61 games for United (Image: PA)

‌



The Toffees were one of several suitors reportedly interested in a move for Romero on deadline day in 2021. However, the Liverpool outfit weren't prepared to pay the supposed £10m price tag attached to the then-34-year-old.

Romero's place in the United pecking order suffered at the time after Dean Henderson returned to the club. That left him and veteran Lee Grant as Ole Gunnar Solskjaer's preferred backups behind De Gea in both the Premier League and Champions League.

"This doesn't sound right to me. It doesn't appear honest or professional or serious that they have to let him go. I am very sad because of this."

Sports.title: Gary Neville jumps to defence of Liverpool icon in 'disrespect' argument with Jamie Carragher
Sports.content:
Gary Neville jumps to defence of Liverpool icon in 'disrespect' argument with Jamie Carragher

Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher clashed during a live segment on Sky Sports while talking about Arsenal striker Kai Havertz and former Liverpool star Roberto Firmino

View 3 Images Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher clashed in a heated segment (Image: Sky Sports )

Gary Neville accused Jamie Carragher of disrespecting former Liverpool striker Roberto Firmino while making a comparison with Arsenal's Kai Havertz.

‌



Havertz has emerged as Mikel Arteta's first-choice forward for the 2026/27 campaign, with the German starting ahead of Viktor Gyokeres so far. The versatile forward, who joined the Gunners from Chelsea for £65million in 2023, scored in the Community Shield win over Manchester City and the 3-0 victory over Coventry on the opening weekend.

‌



The 27-year-old is not a prolific goalscorer, having only once reached double figures in a Premier League season, but his all-round game is highly valued by Arteta. He is sure to have a key role in Arsenal's title defence after they failed to sign a forward in the closing stages of the transfer window.

‌



The Gunners failed to convince Julian Alvarez to return to the Premier League from Atletico Madrid after Real Madrid star Vinicius Junior also turned them down.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Neville feels that, while Havertz is a proven performer for Arsenal, he lacks the star power that they may need. And his opinion, plus a comparison with Liverpool great Firmino, caused a stir in a debate with Carragher on Sky Sports Super Sunday.

Neville: "I think having Havertz up front means the centre-backs can afford to edge over to his side a little bit more, because Havertz is a good player, he's a very good performer, but he's not going to frighten the life out of you."

Carragher: "It didn't stop Mo Salah with Firmino."

‌



Neville: "No, no, no. Please, don't disrespect Firmino in terms of what a player he was by the way."

View 3 Images Kai Havertz is a key player for Arsenal (Image: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Carragher: "In terms of goalscoring."

‌



Neville: "He was unbelievable in the way in which he was a foil for Mane and Salah, it was essential."

Carragher: "So why can't Havertz be that kind of player?"

Neville: "I don't think Havertz is as good as Firmino in any way shape or form."

‌



Firmino returned 111 goals and 76 assists in 362 games over eight years for Liverpool and formed a sensational front line with Sadio Mane and Mohamed Salah. Under Jurgen Klopp's management, the Brazilian won the Premier League, FA Cup, Champions League and Carabao Cup.

View 3 Images Roberto Firmino was a key part of Liverpool's famous front line (Image: PHIL NOBLE, POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

While he played as a No.9, Firmino was known to drop deep, link up play and create space Salah and Mane on the flanks. It is a similar game plan to Arteta at Arsenal, where Havertz leads the line ahead of Christos Tzolis, Bukayo Saka and Martin Odegaard.

‌



Havertz has 38 goals and 18 assists in 114 appearances for Arsenal so far. While Arsenal won their first Premier League title in 22 years last season, he managed seven goals and five assists in all competitions, with just two of those strikes coming in the league.

But having returned from a knee injury, the Germany international will play a key role for the Gunners as they attempt to defend their title.

Sports.title: Jamie Vardy finally decides next club as Leicester icon signs one-year deal
Sports.content:
Jamie Vardy finally decides next club as Leicester icon signs one-year deal

Jamie Vardy will play for Burnley in the Championship this season after finally putting pen to paper on a deal with the Clarets amid speculation over his future

View 2 Images Jamie Vardy has signed for Burnley (Image: Getty Images)

Jamie Vardy has signed for Burnley on a deal until the end of the season.

The Leicester icon, 39, has been without a club since leaving Italian side Cremonese at the end of last season. He had been linked with a shock move to Everton after they failed to land a striker on deadline day.

But Vardy has now penned a deal with Burnley following their relegation from the Premier League.

‌



The Clarets have endured a chastening start in the Championship, mustering just two draws and three defeats from their opening five games, leaving them bottom of the table.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

“I’m really happy to now be here at Burnley FC," he said. "This club has a proper footballing history and passionate fans who deserve a team that represents them and their town.

"I can’t wait to get going on the pitch and help the team move in the right direction.”

Burnley boss Nicky Hayen added: “We are delighted to welcome Jamie to Burnley FC. His experience and leadership will be invaluable to our squad, and we believe he can make a significant impact on our campaign.

"Jamie has a proven track record, and we are looking forward to seeing him in a Claret shirt.”

‌



View 2 Images Vardy in action for Leicester against Sheffield Wednesday (Image: Ben Roberts Photo/Getty Images)

Vardy was the subject of interest from home and abroad following his departure from Cremonese. As well as Everton, boyhood club Sheffield Wednesday were linked as were West Ham, Wrexham and Sao Paolo in Brazil.

Vardy wrote his name into English football folklore by firing Leicester to the most unlikely title win in history in 2016. He also won the FA Cup and two Championship titles with the Foxes.

He played 26 times for England, scoring seven goals.

Sports.title: Arsenal 21-man transfer shortlist as Man City, Chelsea and Liverpool beat them to signings
Sports.content:
Arsenal 21-man transfer shortlist as Man City, Chelsea and Liverpool beat them to signings

Arsenal completed four signings during the summer transfer window, but a report claims the Gunners' 21-man shortlist prepared

View 2 Images Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta (Image: David Price/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Arsenal reportedly had a transfer shortlist prepared for the summer window, but missed out on several deals to their Premier League rivals. One player went to Liverpool in a deal worth more than £100million, while there were several other similar-priced transfers completed.

‌



Mikel Arteta welcomed four new additions to his squad after Arsenal won the Premier League title last season, but did see some departures, too.

‌



Bruno Guimaraes, Ezri Konsa, Christos Tzolis and Illan Meslier were all signed by the reigning league English champions on permanent deals.

‌



Arsenal also sanctioned the exits of Leandro Trossard, Gabriel Martinelli, Gabriel Jesus, Christian Norgaard and Fabio Vieira, who all left on permanent deals.

With the summer transfer window now firmly shut, a report has emerged claiming to reveal the 21 additional players who were on Arsenal's radar ahead of deadline day.

Xabi Alonso confirms Chelsea star's position switch before Arsenal showdown READ MORE :

BBC Sport have reported that Morgan Rogers sat at the very top of Arsenal's wishlist this summer. However, the England international instead completed a £117million switch to Chelsea.

‌



Bradley Barcola also features on the list as a target for the Gunners, before the France international departed Paris Saint-Germain to link up with Liverpool in a deal worth £123million.

Juventus star Kenan Yildiz was named on the list, alongside Yan Diomande, who departed RB Leipzig to join Real Madrid in a blockbuster £120million deal.

Elliot Anderson was also reportedly a target for Arsenal during the summer, with the midfielder ultimately departing Nottingham Forest to sign for Manchester City in a deal valued at £116million.

‌



Sandro Tonali was similarly said to have been on Arsenal's radar before he went on to complete a £100million move to Tottenham Hotspur from Newcastle United.

Vinicius Jr and Julian Alvarez were also both cited as potential Arsenal targets over the summer, though the pair ultimately stayed put at Real Madrid and Atletico Madrid, respectively.

View 2 Images Vinicius Jr. of Real Madrid was linked with a move to Arsenal in the summer (Image: Joaquin Corchero/Europa Press via Getty Images)

‌



FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Eli Junior Kroupi (Bournemouth), Joao Pedro (Chelsea), Alex Scott (Bournemouth), Amadou Onana (Aston Villa), Jeremy Monga (Leicester City to Man City), Louis Page (Leicester City), Cristian Romero (Tottenham to Atletico Madrid) and Micky van de Ven (Tottenham) were amongst the England-based players reportedly wanted by Arsenal.

Nico Paz (Como), Malick Fofana (Lyon to Sunderland), Ivan Fresneda (Sporting Lisbon), Jacobo Ramon (Como) and Tarik Muharemovic (Sassuolo to Leeds) were the overseas-based players said to have featured on the Gunners' transfer shortlist.

‌



Arsenal's next chance to bolster their squad will arrive on New Year's Day, when the January transfer window swings open.

Sports.title: Friendly Soul makes all to strike in Prix Vermeille
Sports.content:
Friendly Soul led from pillar to post to double her Group One tally in the Qatar Prix Vermeille at ParisLongchamp.

A top-level winner in the Prix de l'Opera on Arc weekend two years ago, John and Thady Gosden's five-year-old missed the entirety of last season through injury.

However, she has slowly come to the boil in three starts this term, most recently chasing home Diamond Necklace in the Nassau Stakes at Goodwood.

And although she was tackling a mile and a half for the first time on her return to France, jockey James Doyle did not appear to have any stamina doubts, sending his mount straight to the lead from the off.

Friendly Soul and Composing had built up a healthy lead over the chasing pack rounding the home turn and while both Pink Panthera and Sunly came from further back to mount a late challenge - with the latter perhaps an unlucky loser after missing the break and encountering traffic problems in the straight - the Gosden runner had enough in hand to claim victory.

"It was a hugely sporting decision from her owners, George and Julia Strawbridge, to keep her in training at this age," Thady Gosden told Sky Sports Racing.

"Last time she was here she won the Prix de l'Opera, a couple of years ago now. She likes to do things her own way and took James to the front there, but she didn't get an easy lead at all - she got attacked in the false straight there and was never really able to get a breather.

"Obviously she's a hugely talented filly and very tough too. It's great to have her back to her best."

Friendly Soul is a 16-1 shot for the Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe with Coral. When asked whether Europe's premier middle-distance contest could now be on the agenda, Gosden added: "It was obviously her first time over a mile and a half, so it was slightly unknown territory before this.

"I haven't had a chance to speak to George and Julia yet, we'll see how she comes out of the race and see where they'd like to go with her, but of course it's great to have it (Arc) as an option."

Sports.title: Daryz warms up for Arc with dominant display in Prix Foy
Sports.content:
Daryz looks perfectly placed to defend his Prix de l’Arc de Triomphe crown in four weeks, judged on his dominant display in the Prix Foy.

Francis-Henri Graffard's charge made the perfect start to his four-year-old campaign by winning two more Group Ones at his beloved ParisLongchamp, with a comeback victory in the Prix Ganay followed by a runaway triumph in the Prix Aga Khan IV.

He could only finish third when sent across the Channel for the Prince of Wales's Stakes at Royal Ascot in June, but with connections feeling they had viable excuses for that below-par run, the son of Sea The Stars was expected to regain winning ways back on home turf.

On paper his task was not entirely straightforward, with George Scott's 10-length Coronation Cup winner and fellow Arc aspirant Bay City Roller among his three rivals, and as expected the latter was sent straight to the front by Oisin Murphy in an attempt to draw the sting out of Daryz's exceptional finishing kick.

But Mickael Barzalona always looked ultra-confident in the saddle aboard the red-hot favourite, who cruised alongside Bay City Roller a furlong out and only had to be pushed out hands and heels to win by a length and three-quarters.

"I couldn't be happier with the trial he had today. We got a good lead and luckily Oisin made the pace a little bit harder at the top of the hill, so the horse was really travelling nicely," Graffard told Sky Sports Racing.

"For me as a trainer it was the best preparation I could have for the horse. He will come on a lot for that, I left plenty in him, so he should be spot-on for four weeks' time."

Scott too was delighted with the performance of the runner-up and is hoping for rain in Paris ahead of a rematch with Daryz in Europe's premier middle-distance contest on October 4.

He said: "Oisin was very happy with him and we'll be hoping for a different set of circumstances in a month's time.

"We know that this horse has a high level of form on ground like this, but when it rains he's a different animal.

"He came here and travelled well, went through the race very well and got beaten by a better horse on the day. In four weeks' time that might be the case (again), but it might not, so we'll see.

"I think he's the best version of himself now. The winner might be as well, but in four weeks' time it's going to be completely different.

"He's going to be an underdog coming back, of course he is - Daryz is a champion and he is unbelievable around here. It was all perfect for him today and set up great, but I was very happy with our horse, Oisin was most happy, so we're looking forward to it."

Avec Toi made to work hard to stay unbeaten in Prix la Rochette

Hot favourite Avec Toi was made to pull out all the stops to maintain his unbeaten record in the Qatar Prix la Rochette at ParisLongchamp.

Christopher Head's colt had been hugely impressive in winning his first three starts and was long odds-on to make it four from four in this Group Three contest.

Imperial Strike, winner of his two previous starts for Andre and Lavinia Fabre, made a real race of it and there was little to choose between the pair in the dying strides, but Avec Toi was a short head in front at the line.

Image: Avec Toi (PC. Boudot) wins Qatar Prix La Rochette Gr.3 in ParisLongchamp, France, 06/09/2026, photo: Zuzanna Lupa

A likely rematch between the front two will take place in the Prix Jean-Luc Lagardere in four weeks' time.

Head told Sky Sports Racing: "It was a very nice race with five nice horses. I respected Imperial Strike from the beginning, so I'm very happy our horse won the race and we discovered there's a very nice horse to beat next time too!

"He's a very nice horse and he's done a great job today. It was a pretty tactical race and we are all happy.

"There is a lot to do between the two races and I'm very happy with that."
