Sports.title: Fowler at the double as St Johnstone beat Hibs
Sports.content:
Josh Fowler's first-half double secured St Johnstone a 2-1 win over Hibernian and moved them above their opponents in the table.

Fowler netted from close range on 16 minutes then slotted home a penalty after Nathan Lowe had levelled for Hibs to secure Saints' second win of the campaign.

The visitors were the better team in the second period but Simo Valakari's team held on for a 2-1 success to move into seventh spot.

Fowler, who scored a late equaliser off the bench in midweek at Dundee, fully justified his return to the starting line-up.

The striker scored with the first chance of the contest. Hibs backed off Jason Holt, permitting the Perth captain to reach the 18-yard box and play in Taylor Steven, whose low cross took a nick off the heel of Adam Mayor and landed with Fowler at the back post.

The striker did well to adjust to the deflection and tuck a right-footed finish past Raphael Sallinger.

That good work was undone on 29 minutes by a slack Reece McAlear pass in the centre of the park. Miguel Chaiwa sent Lowe sprinting clear and the on-loan Stoke forward placed a low shot between Toby Steward and his right-hand post.

Image: Hibernian's Nathan Lowe scored to make it 1-1

Saints did well to shrug that mishap off and deservedly retook the lead four minutes from half-time.

Bosnian full-back Enes Alic drove into the penalty box and was nudged over by Martin Boyle. Fowler buried his fourth Premiership goal of the campaign to the bottom right, sending Sallinger the wrong way.

Fowler twice came close to a hat-trick early in the second period, before his 72nd-minute withdrawal.

But it was Hibs who looked most likely to score for large parts of the half.

Kanayo Megwa, who replaced injured Grant Hanley on the hour, met a corner with a powerful back-post header but Steward conjured a brilliant one-handed stop on his line.

Saints brought on Matty Todd and reverted to a back five to see off the threat, although there were some frantic moments of defending.

The hosts were grateful when sub Thibault Klidje struck a good chance off his own man Ante Suto.

Alic forced Sallinger into a fine save as Saints menaced on the break but Valakari's men did enough to see out victory and condemn Hibs to back-to-back defeats.

Sports.title: Kerjota scores dramatic added-time winner as Hearts beat Dundee
Sports.content:
Sabah Kerjota scored a stoppage-time winner as Hearts staged a dramatic late fightback to defeat Dundee 2-1 at Tynecastle and make it four Premiership victories in a row.

Hearts were frustrated for long periods after the visitors - who had both Joe Westley and Fin Robertson stretchered off - took the lead in the 17th minute through Bradley Fink.

But Hearts eventually drew level in the 84th minute through a Claudio Braga penalty before Dundee had Zan Besir sent off as the match ticked into stoppage time.

Wouter Vrancken's buoyant side made their extra man count when Albanian substitute Kerjota drilled in his first goal since arriving at Tynecastle last summer in the sixth minute of added time.

The victory elevated the Jambos, unbeaten in eight in all competitions, to second in the table.

There was one enforced tweak to the Hearts side that started Thursday's Edinburgh derby triumph away to Hibernian as Blair Spittal, who is facing months on the sidelines due to injury, was replaced by Tomas Magnusson.

Dundee boss Steven Pressley made four changes from Wednesday's 1-1 draw with St Johnstone as Imari Samuels, Drey Wright, Robertson and Fink were all added.

Hearts started brightly and Calvin Miller saw an effort deflected behind in the third minute. From the resulting corner, Dundee suffered a blow as Westley had to leave the field on a stretcher after a collision with Jamie McCart. Bobby Wales came on in his place.

The visitors made the breakthrough from their first chance of the match in the 17th minute when Fink got in behind Oisin McEntee to latch on to Samuels' long ball over the top and the Swiss forward looped an effort beyond the exposed Beau Reus from 12 yards.

Image: Dundee's Bradley Fink celebrates after scoring to make it 1-0

Dundee threatened a second when Ethan Hamilton seized on an error from Magnusson and surged forward but his low shot from just outside the box ran wide of Reus' left-hand post.

Hearts, having been knocked out of their rhythm by the visitors in the first half, had a good opportunity five minutes after the break when Josh McPake ran on to Magnusson's pass and drove into the box but he was denied by Owen Goodman.

At the other end, Dundee substitute Jack Moorhouse's shot skimmed the crossbar after he dispossessed Jordi Altena.

Hearts started to crank up the pressure as the half wore on, with James Wilson, Braga, sub JJ Williams and McPake all threatening.

Image: Dundee's Drey Wright (L) and Hearts' Josh McPake (R) battle for possession

Dundee then had a second player stretchered off in the 76th minute when Robertson went down injured.

Hearts eventually levelled in the 84th minute when they were awarded a penalty following a VAR intervention after Owen Bevan was adjudged to have blocked a Christian Borchgrevink cutback with his arm, and Braga stepped up to send Goodman the wrong way.

Dundee suffered further woe in the 90th minute when sub Besir was shown a red card for a reckless challenge on Magnusson, and they were punished again as Kerjota rifled home a low angled finish after a short corner was worked to him just inside the box.

What the result means and next fixtures...

Sports.title: Erdenali shines at top table to claim Prix du Moulin honours
Sports.content:
Erdenali graduated to the highest level in impressive style when proving too strong for the raiding party in the Qatar Prix du Moulin de Longchamp.

A strong British and Irish contingent went to post for the Group One contest, with Aidan O'Brien's Irish 2,000 Guineas hero Gstaad the hot favourite ahead of Charlie Appleby's Opera Ballo and the Ed Walker-trained Ten Bob Tony.

Unlike that trio, Francis-Henri Graffard's Erdenali was unproven in Group One company, but he had looked an exciting prospect in winning his first three starts and was an unlucky loser when third in a Group Three on his most recent outing.

With Opera Ballo taken on for the lead by Gstaad's pacemaker Dorset, Appleby's charge was a spent force entering the final furlong, at which stage Erdenali and the shock Queen Anne winner Ten Bob Tony moved up to dispute the lead.

Erdenali was always getting the better of that particular battle, however, and the pair drew clear of Gstaad, who never threatened to land a telling blow and was ultimately a bit disappointing in third.

Nemone Routh, French racing manager and director for winning owners Aga Khan Studs, told Sky Sports Racing: "We were wondering if he was going to the Arc sale or not after this, but I don't think we will now!

"He's not a horse that shows very much in the morning - if you'd seen him work this week you wouldn't have been particularly impressed, but it all comes together in the afternoon.

"He should have been unbeaten - he should have won that Group Three very easily, we had just a nightmare trip.

"It was always the plan to come here; we needed to find out if he was a Group One horse and I think he's done that quite resoundingly."

Erdenali is Coral's new 2-1 favourite for the Queen Elizabeth II Stakes on Champions Day at Ascot, but with connections fortunate enough to have several horses in the same division, plans are on hold for the time being.

"We have some other horses for the Prix de la Foret - we have Samangan if the ground doesn't get too soft and we have Rayif, who might go to the QEII," Routh added.

"I think Erdenali is in the QEII as well and we were thinking of taking him to Keeneland for a race after this, but we might have to rethink now.

"He's definitely shown us he's a Group One horse."

Walker said of the runner-up Ten Bob Tony: "Thrilled, very proud of him again. I've slightly lost my voice.

"He's amazing and he's had an amazing season. He's really stepped it up a gear, it was a huge run. I'm kind of a bit gutted as I thought we had it. I saw we had Opera Ballo and Gstaad beat and probably didn't give the winner the respect he deserves - he looks very good and we were probably beaten by a very good horse.

"The plan was always the QEII. Whether we do the QEII and the Breeders' Cup, we'll see. We'll do what's right by him, hopefully he'll be around for many more years."

Benvenuto Cellini disappoints as Varandir secures Prix Niel glory

Irish Derby hero Benvenuto Cellini proved bitterly disappointing as Varandir claimed a decisive victory in the Qatar Prix Niel at ParisLongchamp.

Down the field as favourite for the Derby at Epsom before controversially being declared a non-runner due to an incident in the starting stalls, Benvenuto Cellini bounced back to claim Classic glory at the Curragh three weeks later, since when he had finished a creditable third against his elders in the King George at Ascot.

Returning from a short break, the son of Frankel was widely expected to stake his claim for the Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe over the same course and distance in four weeks' time, but after going in pursuit of his pacesetting stablemate Montreal from the home turn, he found little for pressure and weakened into fifth place.

Image: Varandir (M. Barzalona) wins Qatar Prix Niel Gr.2 in ParisLongchamp, France, 06/09/2026, photo: Zuzanna Lupa

With Montreal's petrol tank running on empty entering the final furlong, having streaked clear of his rivals for much of the race, Francis-Henri Graffard's Varandir - a close-up fourth behind the William Haggas-trained Maltese Cross in the Grand Prix de Paris on his last outing - was the one who finished best to grab the lead under Mickael Barzalona and he was ultimately a comfortable winner over the staying-on Alam.

When asked whether the victory was a surprise, Nemone Routh, French racing manager and director for winning owners Aga Khan Studs, told Sky Sports Racing: "No, not hugely. We knew the horse was really well, we knew he'd progressed a lot and we were very happy with his run in the Grand Prix de Paris - he really moved forward from when he won the Group Three and I think he'd moved forward a lot since then.

"He's a horse that mentally and physically has improved throughout the year and we knew we had him well. I think he needed this run, because he was a bit heavy in the preliminaries."

Sports.title: Dunkley hits ton as England clinch ODI series sweep of Ireland
Sports.content:
England secured a 3-0 sweep of Ireland as they won the third and final one-day international of the series by 114 runs in Worcester on Sunday.

Sophia Dunkley (119 off 119 balls) struck a run-a-ball century - her second in ODI cricket - as England set Ireland 292 to win, having been inserted by the visitors.

But Ireland never truly threatened in reply, despite a handful of starts for their top-order batters, as they were ultimately bowled out for 177 after 44.2 overs.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sophia Dunkley completed her second international ODI century in four years after 100 runs from 100 balls against Ireland.

England were also bowled out short of their allotted 50 overs, as the hosts collapsed from 183-1 in the 31st over and 260-4 in the 43rd to 291 all out after 48.5.

It wouldn't prove costly, however, as Lauren Filer (3-27), Mady Villiers (3-33) and Tilly Corteen-Coleman (2-34) starred with the ball to skittle Ireland and secure a series whitewash.

Dunkley continued her fine form with the bat this summer as she cracked 15 boundaries in her sublime knock, sharing in a 73-run opening partnership with Maia Bouchier and dominating a second-wicket century stand with Jodi Grewcock (35).

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ireland badly needed a breakthrough in the third ODI and got one when Kia McCartney forced a leading edge from Maia Bouchier and she was caught on 39.

It laid the foundation for what looked set to be a sizeable score of around 350 or beyond, only for things to fall apart at the back end.

Alice Capsey (10) was run out cheaply, before Dunkley holed out in the deep, and though Dani Gibson (41 off 37) and Freya Kemp (23 off 21) cracked a few lusty blows in a 46-run partnership for the fifth wicket, England lost 6-31 in the space of little more than six overs thereafter.

Ireland captain Gaby Lewis claimed a terrific catch on the long-off boundary to see the back of Kemp and trigger the collapse, with leg-spinner Cara Murray (4-56) claiming a career-first four-for.

Filer (16) dismissed Lewis early on in the Ireland reply, before Alice Tector (29) and Amy Hunter (39) laid the foundations with a 56-run second-wicket stand - but too slowly.

The tourists began to fall behind the required rate, and there was only to be one winner when the wickets began to tumble.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Rookie wicket keeper Alice Capsey showed she is learning fast by taking two stumpings in the third ODI against Ireland.

Corteen-Coleman first bowled Tector, Capsey then claimed a couple of stumpings - Hunter and Rebecca Stokell (14) - to continue her successful wicketkeeping audition in this series, before Orla Prendergast (24) was caught at deep midwicket.

Corteen-Coleman then cleaned up another batter, Louise Little (14), as Ireland lost their last five wickets for 10 runs in under four overs - Filer finishing off the job by dismantling Kia McCartney's stumps.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England Women's national selector Lydia Greenway reflects on the team's 2026 summer and how they are trying to tighten the gap on Australia.

Dunkley: I want to open in all formats

Player of the series and match Sophia Dunkley:

"It was just great to get the series win today.

"It was definitely tricky at the start. The longer you batted the easier it got. It was nice to get through that period and see us home.

"For me, it is just about staying really present. I love batting for whatever team I am playing for and it is great to be at the top of the order again in ODI cricket.

"It is definitely my goal to be at the top of the order in all formats."

Farrant: Dunkley completed her goal

Sky Sports Cricket's Tash Farrant:

"Dunkley has scored big runs.

"We all know she can get off to fast and furious starts. The main goal for her this series will have been match-winning contributions.

"She wanted big runs and she has done that today."

Sports.title: Maitland-Niles stunner rescues late point for Everton against Manchester United
Sports.content:
It would be putting it mildly to say Everton’s exhaustive search for a new right-back met an underwhelming response when it concluded with the signing of Ainsley Maitland-Niles on Monday. But there was an overwhelmingly positive reaction to the £4.3m recruit’s Everton debut as his stunning 25-yard strike rescued a point with virtually the final kick of the game against Manchester United.

Michael Carrick wiped his face in sheer disbelief after the former Arsenal player, 19 minutes into his first appearance for David Moyes’s side, found Senne Lammens’ top corner to send Hill Dickinson Stadium into raptures at the end of a troubled week. United were on the verge of victory following Benjamin Sesko’s 88th-minute header beyond Jordan Pickford but Everton, indignant and defiant after the shambles of transfer deadline day, twice fought back to preserve their unbeaten start to the season. A slow-burning contest erupted into a wildly entertaining second half.

The response to Everton’s transfer deadline day was muted and so was the start to the contest. Hill Dickinson was shorn of the tifos and flag displays usually organised by The 1878s, the supporters group who have withdrawn their support for the foreseeable future, and there were attempts to organise a ‘not a pound in the ground’ protest to hit the owners where they would feel it. But there were no visible or audible shows of dissent against TFG inside the ground. Not that anyone from Everton’s ownership group was here to witness any beyond Rishi Majithia, Dan Friedkin’s son-in-law and TFG’s day-to-day representative at the club. They missed practically nothing before half-time.

Harry Maguire was left with a bloody nose following an aerial challenge with Thierno Barry in the opening seconds. The contest and the atmosphere took a long time to recover from the lengthy break for the defender to receive treatment.

United went close early on when Bruno Fernandes cushioned a volley against the Everton crossbar from Bryan Mbeumo’s knock-down. Luke Shaw engineered the chance by breaking free down the left and picking out Mbeumo inside the area. It should have been a fruitful route for the visitors with Shaw and Marcus Rashford frequently getting in behind Merlin Röhl but, in keeping with the performance of both teams before the break, an end product was lacking. Matheus Cunha had the best opportunity from a low Rashford delivery, dummied by Diogo Dalot, but sidefooted wastefully over from 18 yards.

Moyes rightly persisted with Röhl at right-back despite the addition of Maitland-Niles. The Germany under-21 international is now considered a potential long-term solution to Everton’s problematic position and his early season displays merited the manager’s trust. Defensively this was a difficult but valuable experience for Röhl, who demonstrated his usefulness in the final third with a fine cross that Barry headed over from close range having pulled away from Maguire. That was Everton’s one chance of note in a forgettable half.

View image in fullscreen Benjamin Sesko heads Manchester United into the lead from close range in the 88th minute. Photograph: Jason Cairnduff/Action Images/Reuters

United were the more composed and creative side, without seriously troubling Pickford after Fernandes struck the bar, but finally added penetration to their performance 62 seconds after the restart. Everton were collectively still asleep when the breakthrough arrived. Receiving Kobbie Mainoo’s pass wide on the right, Mbeumo set off in a straight line for the Everton goal, darting between nonexistent challenges from Tyrique George and Vitalii Mykolenko before sweeping an excellent finish beyond Pickford’s despairing dive as James Garner sat off on the edge of the area.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

A superbly timed challenge from James Tarkowski prevented Cunha converting into an empty net from Rashford’s backheel. It looked a key moment when Everton, having passed up several presentable chances from Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall, Harrison Armstrong and Brennan Johnson, equalised from out of nowhere with seven minutes of normal time remaining. George was found in space on the right by the substitute Hayden Hackney and unleashed an unstoppable shot into the near, top corner of Lammens’ goal from a ridiculously tight angle.

It was the parity Everton’s second-half improvement deserved but United finally profited from one of their raids down the left to retake the lead shortly afterwards. Sesko started and finished the move when, having benefited from a kind bounce off Hackney, he found Fernandes in space. The United captain released Shaw on Maitland-Niles and his perfectly weighted cross sailed over Tarkowski for Sesko to score with a textbook header past Pickford. Sesko’s header trickled over the line after the Everton keeper got a hand to the ball. The final sting, however, would come from Everton and their new, previously unheralded right-back.

Sports.title: Embattled Fifa president Infantino declares intention to stand for re-election
Sports.content:
The Fifa president, Gianni Infantino, has reiterated his desire to stand for re-election next year despite the continuing controversy surrounding his leadership.

Infantino refused to answer questions about his future when asked by reporters at the Women’s Under-20 World Cup in Poland on Saturday. The 56-year-old Swiss is under severe pressure to resign after trying to sell stakes in Fifa tournaments, including the World Cup, to private investors.

Uefa, the European governing body, has led calls for Infantino to step down with further opposition coming from the Asian confederation and Concacaf, which represents countries in North and Central America plus the Caribbean.

But for the first time since the plan became public, Fifa has reiterated Infantino’s intention to run for a fourth and final term in next year’s elections. Should he be re-elected, he will continue to serve as head of world football until 2031.

A Fifa spokesperson said: “The Fifa president announced in April that he will stand for re-election in 2027. Of course, nothing has changed. Mr Infantino will be standing for re-election.”

The Concacaf president, Victor Montagliani, is widely seen as the likeliest challenger to Infantino. Montagliani, a Fifa vice-president, had long been regarded as a close ally of Infantino, but there were signs, even before he distanced himself over the now-scrapped plan to allow private investment into World Cups, that he viewed Fifa’s purpose somewhat differently to the Swiss.

However, Infantino is not without friends – Saudi Arabia, the 2034 men’s World Cup hosts, came out in support last month, with African football’s governing body, Caf, and South America’s Conmebol also supportive.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Sport in Focus Our picture editors select their favourite sporting images from the past week, from the spectacular to the powerful, and with a little bit of fun thrown in Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

As the only declared candidate so far for the election due to take place in March 2027, Infantino will need a simple majority of votes from the 211 federations affiliated to Fifa to extend his term of office, which began in 2016. Candidate nominations for next year’s election must be submitted by 18 November.

Sports.title: Armstrong spurns golden chance to win derby as Birmingham and Wolves draw
Sports.content:
If only Adam Armstrong, the Wolves striker presented with a golden chance in the 87th minute, had shot into the same corner of the net at the Railway End that his teammate ­Jackson Tchatchoua had located when scoring one of the most ­memorable own goals at the end of the first half, then César Peixoto’s team would surely now be second in the Championship.

Instead Armstrong, one of the Football League’s most proven goalscorers, lifted his shot over an open goal from 10 yards when played in by Fer López at the end of this implausibly open derby. Birmingham ultimately deserved to extend their unbeaten start to the league season.

After their 4-2 defeat at West Ham on Tuesday, Wolves look as vulnerable defensively as they can be devas­tating going forward. Only Burnley, relegated with them last season, have conceded more than their 10 goals.

Tom Wagner, the ­Birmingham chair, was back in the St Andrew’s directors’ box for the first time since a stroke in February and was treated to a thrilling game. Spoils were shared but Chris Davies was happy with his side after they twice came from behind. “I’ll always be content when the players put in that heart and spirit,” the ­Birmingham manager said. “When you look at the quality of their team, I’ll be astonished if they’re not in the top four. Second half, we put them to the sword.”

López scored in the third ­minute for Wolves and, after Jay ­Stansfield equalised in controversial circum­stances, Ladislav Krejci gave the visitors the lead again. But then came the moment that could haunt ­Tchatchoua. The Cameroon right‑back was under no pressure as he went to turn a long diagonal from Phil Neumann back towards his ­goalkeeper – but instead looped the ball wide and over José Sá into his own goal.

That moment set the tempo for the rest of a game. Wolves, despite ­retaining the majority of their ­Premier League squad after the transfer deadline, know sheer quality of player alone will not mean promotion.

Peixoto called for video assistant referees to be brought in to the Championship after Stansfield appeared to handle when bringing down Patrick Roberts’s brilliant chip before hammering home Birmingham’s first equaliser. “If the referee doesn’t see it, then what can you do?” Stansfield said.

Peixoto said: “I don’t know why they don’t have VAR in the Champion­ship. It’s very important to help the refe­rees to take the best decisions. I saw a handball and in the screen we saw a handball.” The ­Portuguese coach also confirmed that in a pre‑season meeting with Professional Game Match Officials Limited (PGMOL), ­managers were told that grappling at corners would be penalised. “But it’s not happening,” he said.

View image in fullscreen Adam Armstrong (left) reacts to his missed chance to win it for Wolves at Birmingham. Photograph: Nick Potts/PA

While the home side dominated the second half, Wolves could have put the game to bed before Birmingham got going. López was involved in the buildup before advancing to side‑foot home Rodrigo Gomes’s right‑wing cross to the near post for his third goal of the season.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Then in the 19th minute, ­Christoph Klarer’s poor touch invited Raúl ­Jiménez to steal the ball and put in Gomes who allowed James ­Beadle to save his dinked attempt.

Krejci is one of the elite players surprisingly still at Wolves. The Czechia captain’s bullet header, after André flicked on Hugo Bueno’s corner, gave Wolves another endorphin boost. It was short-lived, however, as Tchatchoua lobbed home his tragicomic own goal. Jiménez hit the crossbar, as he did in defeat at West Ham, but then Neumann headed against the same woodwork midway through the second half.

Wolves had the clearest of many chances both teams had to win the game. López dispossessed Demarai Gray inside the area and, faced with the goalkeeper, squared for ­Armstrong. Somehow he contrived to lift the ball over the empty goal. “The way Jack[son Tchatchoua] committed his mistake, Adam committed the mistake in the opposite side,” Peixoto said. “We have to take the confidence to them and keep fighting and work hard for the next game.”

There was still time for ­Birmingham to think they had won it as Marvin Ducksch arced a free-kick towards the top corner. There, however, was Sá to show why he was awarded a new contract, as he tipped the ball aside to ensure this pulsating match finished even.

Sports.title: Jamie Vardy takes party to Burnley after signing deal with Championship strugglers
Sports.content:
Jamie Vardy has returned to English football after signing for Burnley in the Championship as a free agent.

Vardy, who will be 40 in January, has signed a contract until the end of the season, having spent last season at Cremonese in Italy. A return to Leicester, where he spent 13 years and was a Premier League champion in 2016 and an FA Cup winner in 2021, was mooted in the summer, only for Vardy to rule out a reunion.

His podcast, Jamie Vardy’s Having A Party, made the news last week for Mike Dean’s lifting of the lid on his antics as a Premier League referee and has secured broadcast rights for a Bundesliga watch-along. He has also, with his wife Rebekah, starred in an ITV reality series, and been the subject of a Netflix documentary.

Despite those wider interests, Vardy’s intention has been to carry on playing, having been a late starter, making his Football League debut at 25 after signing for Leicester.

Burnley were relegated from the Premier League last term and, with Nicky Hayen as their manager, remain without a win after their opening five games of the Championship campaign, losing to Bristol City on Saturday. Vardy joins a team bottom of the division.

“This club has a proper footballing history and passionate fans who deserve a team that represents them and their town,” Vardy said. “I can’t wait to get going on the pitch and help the team move in the right direction.”

In June, he said of Leicester, now in League One, currently struggling under the management of Russell Martin: “I think that’s gone. I’ll always support them, always follow them. I think that’s the best thing I can do now.”

Sports.title: Glasner claims VAR was ‘guessing’ after Forest are denied winner against Spurs
Sports.content:
Oliver Glasner argued there was insufficient evidence to disallow Neco Williams’s goal against Tottenham, accusing the video assistant referee Peter Bankes of guessing that the Nottingham Forest defender handled and said ruling it out weakens the officials’ authority. Midway through the second half, Williams stooped to head in on the goalline as Sandro Tonali attempted to hook the ball clear after Morgan Gibbs-White’s deflected effort bobbled towards the net.

Glasner conceded at least one angle showed Williams appeared to handle the ball, seemingly to protect himself as Tonali went to clear the ball with his left boot, but said the footage was too unclear to disallow the goal. “I don’t think VAR can intervene when he’s guessing,” said Forest’s head coach. “It was not clear and obvious. We had a briefing before the season that the threshold for VAR intervention should be very high and this is why it was a wrong intervention for me.

“I’ve watched five or six different angles and to be fair, from one angle you can guess that the ball touched the arm because the shirt [of Williams] moves a little bit, but it’s not clear whether it’s [because of] the ball or Tonali on the goalline. I know refereeing a Premier League game is really difficult – refereeing a training session is sometimes really difficult – but we are told to support the referee, to keep the threshold for VAR intervention very high, to strengthen the referee’s decision and they didn’t do that today. With these kinds of situations, you weaken the referees.”

Bankes checked the goal and then the referee, Craig Pawson, took to the mic before awarding a Spurs free-kick amid a chorus of boos from the home support: “After review, the ball touches the hand of Nottingham Forest’s No 3 before the goal is scored.” Williams was adamant he did not handle the ball. “I headed it in between my arms,” said the Wales defender, who this week signed a new four-year contract. “If you’re going to pause it, it’s going to look like it hit my arm but it didn’t. I have seen all the images and at not one moment can you tell that has clearly hit my arms because it never. I knew straight away I’d headed it down in between my arms.”

The disallowed goal was undeniably the moment of an underwhelming contest. For the third successive league match, Tottenham failed to score and this time they did not even muster a shot on target. Dominic Solanke heading on to the roof of the Forest goal, 88 minutes on the clock, was as threatening as they got. Omar Marmoush wellied a shot wide after Spurs countered at speed. Mykhailo Mudryk was brought off the bench for his first competitive minutes for 645 days after a doping suspension but Spurs were blunt. Aside from a 5-1 win against a Charlton B team in the Carabao Cup, their season so far reads: five goals against and none scored.

View image in fullscreen Spurs’ Mykhailo Mudryk came on as a late substitute for his first competitive appearance for 645 days. Photograph: Andrew Boyers/Action Images/Reuters

Apart from Gibbs-White’s effort in the buildup to the disallowed goal, Forest’s only other shot on goal was a daisy-cutter from James McAtee. The Spurs league debutant Sávio, a £75m arrival from Manchester City, showed a few neat touches but he and Destiny Udogie were withdrawn after an hour on the advice of Tottenham’s medical department. “I’m not happy when we have the plan but it is for my advantage, my business, the management of the players after their injuries,” said De Zerbi, who accepted his team lacked quality in the final third. “We have to make better decisions, to keep more calm when we are very close to do something important.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

No wonder both teams remain winless. Spurs’s date at home to Everton next weekend has taken on another layer of significance and the same applies to Forest’s trip to Aston Villa. Vinai Venkatesham, the Tottenham chief executive in attendance, could be forgiven for wondering when Spurs will see the fruits of their £300m-plus spend, much of the focus on sharpening their attack. They turned to Mudryk, who thrived under De Zerbi at Shakhtar Donetsk, after the failure to sell Richarlison halted moves for preferred targets Cody Gakpo and Iliman Ndiaye. This was not the desired result. “We bought very, very good players but you can’t just build the team with the names like in Football Manager,” De Zerbi said.

Sports.title: High-flying Hull stay unbeaten by holding off Aston Villa in stalemate
Sports.content:
It’s never dull in Hull, as the saying goes in these parts, and after just three games the Premier League is proving to be quite some ride for Hull City supporters.

Having embarrassed Manchester United here on the opening day and won at Coventry last weekend, this deserved point and third successive clean sheet merely reinforced Sergej Jakirovic’s belief that his men can beat the drop.

You have to go back to Bolton’s excellent start in 2001-02 to find a promoted side who began the season with three straight victories. The Tigers failed to emulate Sam Allardyce’s team, but they came closest to a winner as the Algeria winger Mohamed Belloumi hit the crossbar with a stunning second-half shot before the substitute Mohamed-Ali Cho and Oli McBurnie threatened late on.

“We could have won, but they also had a few chances in the second half,” said Jakirovic, who signed a two-year contract extension on Friday. “We won’t be ungrateful for seven points after three games and another clean sheet. It’s a great result for us and we showed we can compete at this level.”

For Aston Villa, it was another largely impotent display which saw them fail to score for the third match running as the captain, John McGinn, and Emiliano Buendía spurned decent second-half opportunities.

Villa failed to manage a shot on target when being hammered 4-0 at Brighton and losing 1-0 at home to Arsenal; here they managed just one, a tame shot by George Hemmings early on.

Unai Emery chose to take the positives from Villa’s display as he patiently rebuilds the club after a summer of major upheaval which saw a number of key players leave and 10 new faces arrive.

View image in fullscreen George Hemmings had Aston Villa’s first shot on target of the Premier League season, 13 minutes into their third game. Photograph: Craig Brough/Action Images/Reuters

“The result is not enough, but I think we deserved more,” he said. “We weren’t clinical but of course to win matches, you need goals. We created chances today to score and we must improve but we are rebuilding.”

Ambition pulsed loudly at a sold-out MKM Stadium before kick-off as a huge amber banner inscribed with the words “One family, one dream” was paraded on the pitch. It said much for the togetherness that Jakirovic has fashioned within his squad and the connection with the club’s supporters during a remarkable few months in the Tigers’ history.

Desire was visible and audible in the stands and on the pitch, but Villa almost led inside the second minute when Nicolas Jackson headed Ian Maatsen’s teasing left-wing cross wastefully wide.

Hull were unfazed and Belloumi beat Ross Barkley twice, including with a delightful nutmeg, before breaking clear down the right flank. His low cross was cleared, but it hinted at the possibilities on offer for the hosts.

In the 13th minute, Villa finally fashioned their only effort on target this season as Hemmings’s low shot was comfortably saved by Konstantinos Tzolakis.

If Villa could not see off a promoted side widely tipped for an immediate relegation this season, could they really consider themselves ready to start climbing the table? A neat passing sequence should have brought a Villa goal in the 50th minute but McGinn could only lift the ball harmlessly over Tzolakis’s crossbar from less than 12 yards out.

Three minutes later, Villa went even closer as Hemmings outstripped the Hull captain, Lewie Coyle, down the left flank and showed intelligence to pick out Buendía with a neat cut-back. Buendía should have buried the chance but he blazed wildly over, much to his disgust.

In the 65th minute, Hull went agonisingly close to scoring when Belloumi collected possession from a short corner and curled a stunning left-foot shot against the bar. There was a resilience to the hosts, and the collective desire that carried them to promotion last season will be needed over the next 35 games if they are to defy the odds and beat the drop.

It was evident again late on when the Hull substitute Lucas Herrington – on his 19th birthday – produced a vital block to repel Tyrone Mings’s shot. Cho’s close-range effort was then repelled by Zion Suzuki before McBurnie failed to properly connect with Giles’s cross as Hull looked likeliest to nick a late winner.

Sports.title: ‘I’ll expose this league’ – Cristiano Ronaldo’s teammate makes shock statement after defeat
Sports.content:
Al Nassr's first league defeat of the season has been met with a furious reaction by one of their star players.

The reigning Saudi Pro League champions lost 2-1 at Al Ittihad on Sunday with a brace from George Ilenikhena giving the hosts all three points despite Angelo Gabriel pulling one back for the visitors.



3 Cristiano Ronaldo's Al Nassr suffered their first defeat of the season on Saturday Credit: Getty

It ended a run of seven matches unbeaten in the league dating back to last season.

Al Nassr had not tasted defeat since losing to Al Qadsiah on May 3.

Whilst Cristiano Ronaldo played the full 90 minutes, it was his compatriot Joao Felix who was left enraged at full time.

The forward unleashed an angry outburst as he made his way back to the team bus.



Felix had been booked for a foul during the second half by referee Khalid Saleh Al Turais.

He appeared to still be frustrated as he made his way through the mixed zone after the final whistle.



Having refused to speak to reporters, video footage from the mixed zone captured Felix explaining his decision.

The 26-year-old was caught on camera stating: "I won't speak to you, if I do, I'll expose the league."



Felix joined Al Nassr from Chelsea last summer on an initial two-year deal.

He has since scored 30 goals and added 22 assists in 53 appearances across all competitions.

3 Felix refused to speak to reporters in the mixed zone at full-time Credit: Getty

Those include two goals in the league already this season for Al Nassr, who had made a perfect start under Ange Postecoglou.



The former Tottenham Hotspur manager was appointed in July as Jorge Jesus' successor.

His side's defeat on Saturday leaves them three points adrift of leaders Al Hilal.

Their title rivals remain unbeaten with five wins from five matches this season.

Al Nassr will have the opportunity to bounce back at home to Abha on Wednesday night.



They then travel to take on Al Khaleej on Saturday. Neither of their next two opponents have picked up a win yet five matches into the campaign.

Sports.title: Gabriel avoids red card for boot in face of Emi Martinez as Premier League gives explanation
Sports.content:
Gabriel avoids red card for boot in face of Emi Martinez as Premier League gives explanation

Gabriel escaped a red card during the first half of Arsenal's clash against Chelsea after clashing with Emi Martinez.

The Gunners defender appeared to kick out at the opposition goalkeeper following a free-kick.



3 This challenge from Gabriel on Martinez went unpunished

Martin Odegaard's low delivery created a goal-mouth scramble inside the six-yard box.

Gabriel had gone to ground as he tussled for the ball with Jorrel Hato.

Gabriel kicks Martinez's face

However, in his attempts to prod the ball towards goal, his boot connected with Martinez's face.



The World Cup winner was left requiring treatment after he had stayed down in agony.

Replays showed Gabriel had made contact as he swiped his leg at the ball whilst on the floor.



He escaped punishment for his rash antics, though, with referee Chris Kavanagh not brandishing a card.

Why was Gabriel not sent off?

His on-field decision was supported by VAR following a check of the incident.



Had the review deemed Gabriel had exhibited serious foul play, the Brazil international would have been sent off.

It came just minutes after Chelsea had raced into an early lead at the Emirates Stadium.

Morgan Rogers' effort in the second minute opened the scoring.

3 Gabriel kicked Martinez in the face following an Arsenal free-kick Credit: Getty

Arsenal thought they had equalised through Riccardo Calafiori ten minutes later.



However, his strike was ruled out due to an offside against Ezri Konsa earlier in the move.

Despite the disallowed effort, the Gunners were level before the break thanks to Kai Havertz's equaliser.

Gabriel has previously been sent off twice for Arsenal in 265 appearances for the club.

Since his arrival from Lille in 2020, he has also been shown 32 yellow cards.



Both of his dismissals came as second yellows cards after earlier being cautioned.

3 Havertz's goal pulled Arsenal level before half time Credit: Getty

The most recent of those occurred during a 2-1 home defeat to Manchester City in January 2022.

Having already been booked for dissent, Gabriel was sent off just two minutes later after a second yellow card.

Sports.title: Karim Benzema return to former club collapses despite Ballon d’Or winner agreeing to play for free
Sports.content:
Karim Benzema return to former club collapses despite Ballon d’Or winner agreeing to play for free

Karim Benzema came close to rejoining former club Lyon this summer, but his transfer from Al Hilal collapsed.

The deal did not get completed despite the 2022 Ballon d'Or winner offering to return to France and play for free.

3 Benzema offered to rejoin hometown club Lyon and play for free Credit: Getty

Benzema was willing to play for his hometown side again without a salary, according to L'Equipe.

However, at the time the Ligue 1 club were considering an approach, he was still under contract in Saudi Arabia.

The Real Madrid legend has since had his deal terminated just six months after joining Al Hilal from Al Ittihad.

He departed the club after they announced the signing of Ollie Watkins from Aston Villa.

It means that Benzema is now a free agent, but a move to Lyon reportedly remains 'impossible'.

Why did Benzema not join Lyon?

L'Equipe have revealed that his contract as an ambassador for the Saudi Pro League is preventing him from a transfer.

His deal is still in place until 2030 and he is keen to honour it, making a move back to his former club extremely difficult.

The PIF have Benzema's image rights and there have been no negotiations with Ligue 1, as reaching agreement over an exception would have been 'nearly impossible'.

Due to that, it has been reported that the former France international could end up deciding to retire.

The 38-year-old will be 43 by the end of his Saudi contract.

3 Benzema played for Lyon at the start of his career, coming through their academy Credit: Getty

Benzema denied dream return

So, Benzema won't be joining Lyon for a second stint at the club in which he started his successful career.

The striker played 148 games for the French giants' first team after coming through their academy system from 1997.

He scored 66 goals and provided 25 assists before leaving to join Real Madrid in 2009.

Of course, Benzema would go on to win the Ballon d'Or as a Real player, also becoming a club legend in Spain.

He played 648 games for the club - the fifth-highest ever for Los Blancos - scoring 354 goals and sitting below only Cristiano Ronaldo in their all-time history of goalscorers.

Benzema left Madrid for Saudi Arabia in 2023 after 14 years, going on to win one league title, two cups and Player of the Year with Al Ittihad.

3 Benzema's Saudi contract means he'll struggle to find a new team Credit: Getty

But after turning down a contract and leaving Al Ittihad for Al Hilal last summer, his career took a downturn.

Hilal manager Simone Inzaghi's decision to bring in another striker, Watkins, left Benzema unhappy and he mutually terminated his contract amid plans to be left out of their league squad.

He scored 10 goals and assisted five in just 16 appearances.

Roberto De Zerbi is not sweating over Tottenham's poor start to the season - despite Saturday's 0-0 draw away at Nottingham Forest.

Sports.title: FIFA president Gianni Infantino to stand for re-election despite controversies
Sports.content:
FIFA president Gianni Infantino to stand for re-election despite controversies

FIFA has confirmed Gianni Infantino will stand for re-election as president.

The 56-year-old has been under mounting pressure since his failed bid to sell stakes in the World Cup.



3 Infantino is going for another term as president despite huge uncertainty over his future Credit: AFP

Prior to this summer's tournament, he had been expected to be re-elected unopposed.

A host of governing bodies have withdrawn their support for his campaign, including the FA.

They had previously given their backing to his re-election bid.

Meanwhile, UEFA have held talks over a vote of no confidence in Infantino.



The confederation previously announced it would boycott the World Cup if his FIFA Forward Enterprise plan went ahead.

Infantino's proposal would have seen private equity in FIFA tournaments sold.



Despite the backlash to his now abandoned plans, the Swiss lawyer is set to contest the next election.

The 77th FIFA Congress in March will see the presidential election take place in Rabat, Morocco.



FIFA statement

In a statement confirming the news, FIFA said: "The FIFA President announced in April that he will stand for re-election in 2027.

"Of course, nothing has changed. Mr Infantino will be standing for re-election."

3 Infantino has been under mounting pressure over his failed FIFA Forward Enterprise plans Credit: AFP

As it stands, no other candidates have declared their intention to run against Infantino next year.



CONCACAF president Victor Montagliani is actively considering running, though.

The Canadian has been in his current role since 2016 and is a current FIFA vice-president.

As for Infantino, he succeeded Sepp Blatter as FIFA president in February 2016.

His two subsequent re-election bids have seen him stand unopposed in both 2019 and 2023.



However, his hopes of landing a third and final full term are currently in the balance.

3 Infantino is currently set to run unopposed in March's FIFA presidential election Credit: AFP

talkSPORT understands UEFA is preparing to begin criminal proceedings against Infantino.

If re-elected, he would remain FIFA president until 2031 after his last four-year term.

Sports.title: Wrexham boss Phil Parkinson left shocked after ‘leg-breaking challenge’
Sports.content:
Wrexham manager Phil Parkinson has slammed a 'leg-breaking challenge' from Swansea's Ben Cabango during their derby.

Parkinson believes Cabango should have been sent off for a reckless tackle on Callum O'Hare in the 77th minute of the game.

3 Cabango was booked for clattering O'Hare in the final stages of the derby Credit: Getty

The two Welsh sides faced off on Saturday evening, with the clash eventually ending 0-0, but things could have been different in the final stages should a red card have been handed out.

Cabango launched into a tackle on O'Hare, missing the ball and taking out the Red Dragons' new £6.5million signing.

The angry Wrexham bench cleared after the aggressive challenge, which left O'Hare rolling around on the floor in pain.

However, Cabango was only shown a yellow card, much to the confusion and disappointment of Parkinson.

"I know we want to protect our players but, when someone flies in at that speed, that could have been a leg-breaking challenge," he said.

"I thought the referee handled the atmosphere well, but in the big decision he didn't make the right call.

"I don't think anybody in the ground or people watching back on TV can deny that."

Parkinson: 'That is a straight red card'

Parkinson went on to compare Cabango's tackle to a red card handed to Wrexham's Callum Doyle last season, questioning why such an 'out of control' challenge didn't lead to a sending off too.

"Cabango grabbed Kieffer [Moore] around the neck on the halfway line before that," he added. "A yellow card and then the tackle.

"The same referee sent Callum Doyle off against Oxford last season for a tackle, which maybe he was slightly out of control.

3 Parkinson has been left raging that the 'leg-breaking' tackle didn't lead to a red Credit: Getty

"But I'm very interested to ask the referee when he compares both those incidents how he differentiates between the two.

"Because every year, managers have to sit and listen to the referees about what they deem to be red cards, and when you're out of control, like Ben Cabango was, and endangering a player.

"That is a straight red card."

What next for Wrexham and Swansea?

A sending off for Cabango may have given Wrexham the chance to claim a late winner against a 10-man Swansea.

But in the end, the game ended goalless and that left Parkinson's side sitting 11th in the Championship table.

They have drawn three of their opening five games, winning 3-0 against Millwall in midweek for their first victory.

3 Swansea remained top of the Championship after the 0-0 draw with Wrexham Credit: Getty

As for Swansea, they remained top of the second tier after an impressive start, winning three and drawing two games so far.

Vitor Matos' side sit above Middlesbrough and Queens Park Rangers, having conceded only one goal in their five matches.

Swansea and Wrexham will meet again on April 7, 2027.

Sports.title: Jamie Vardy completes English football return with shock Championship club
Sports.content:
Burnley have announced the signing of free agent Jamie Vardy on a contract until the end of the season.

Vardy had been without a club all summer following his departure from Italian side Cremonese at the end of last term.

2 Vardy has signed for Burnley to mark his return to English football Credit: Getty

The Premier League-winning Leicester City legend had been linked with Everton and Wrexham during the transfer window.

Sheffield Wednesday and Brazilian side Sao Paolo also appeared as potential next clubs for the ex-England international.

However, out of nowhere, Burnley confirmed the arrival of 39-year-old Vardy in a shock announcement made on Sunday.

On his move, Vardy said: “I’m really happy to now be here at Burnley.

"This club has a proper footballing history and passionate fans who deserve a team that represents them and their town.

"I can’t wait to get going on the pitch and help the team move in the right direction.”

Burnley head coach Nicky Hayen added: "We are delighted to welcome Jamie to Burnley FC.

"His experience and leadership will be invaluable to our squad, and we believe he can make a significant impact on our campaign.

"Jamie has a proven track record, and we are looking forward to seeing him in a Claret shirt."

Vardy's move to Turf Moor caught many off guard following the transfer deadline, with talkSPORT's Perry Groves describing the switch as a 'curveball'.

Vardy returns to England

Vardy will be back playing in the EFL this season after joining Burnley a year after leaving Leicester at the end of his contract.

The veteran striker left the King Power Stadium in April 2025, having played 500 games and scored 200 goals for the club.

He won the Premier League, FA Cup and Community Shield across 13 years, also playing in the Champions League.

But after leaving, he headed for Italy in a surprise move, spending a year in Serie A with Cremonese and playing 29 games.

Vardy scored seven goals during his spell, which ended after just a year following the club's relegation to Serie B.

And that left him as a free agent, with him now returning to the Championship, where he has played 98 times and scored 38 goals previously, following a summer of transfer rumours.

2 Vardy left Leicester last year but he's now back in England with Burnley Credit: Getty

Burnley boost

Burnley have added Vardy to their ranks after losing frontman Zian Flemming to Ipswich on Deadline Day.

The Clarets are in desperate need of some positivity after making a terrible start to the Championship season.

Hayen's side sit bottom of the table after five games, only picking up two points so far following relegation last term.

They were beaten 2-1 by Bristol City on Saturday, on an afternoon that saw Armando Broja clash with fans post-match.

Vardy's arrival though, will likely give them a boost as they aim to turn things around this season.

He has scored nine goals against Burnley in his career, but now he will be hoping to score plenty for them.

Sports.title: Crystal Palace star has perfect response to Fulham fan heckle
Sports.content:
Ben Chilwell chirped back at a Fulham fan following his perfect Premier League return for Crystal Palace on Saturday.

Chilwell scored a late winner for Palace just a few days after joining the club, before post-match footage showed him basking in the glory during an interaction with a supporter.



2 Chilwell scored the winner for Palace and had the last laugh with a supporter Credit: Getty

The left-back smashed home a rebound only three minutes after being substituted on to claim a 3-2 win for the Eagles.

He wheeled away in celebration at the time, screaming in joy in front of the away fans as Fulham sank to a third straight loss.

Alvaro Arbeloa's side sit joint-bottom of the Premier League after the loss, but that didn't stop a fan digging at Chilwell.



A Cottagers supporter shouted down towards Chilwell from the stands as he walked down the tunnel at Craven Cottage.

The fan shouted: "Chelsea reject!"

Chilwell instantly responded to the chirp, saying 'Take that L' and holding his fingers up in an L shape towards the supporter.



Silence followed from the Fulham fan, with another person in the background of the video, which was posted by Crystal Palace's official account, chanting: "Wheyyyyy!"

Chilwell spent five years as a Chelsea player after joining from Leicester in a deal worth up to £50million in 2020.



He won the Champions League at the club and played over 100 games, scoring nine goals and providing 13 assists.

However, he did miss 110 matches due to injury and his Blues career fizzled out in 2024, joining Palace on loan before then leaving Stamford Bridge permanently last summer.

2 Chilwell played over 100 games for Chelsea but is now back in a Palace shirt Credit: Getty

Chilwell: 'I'm buzzing'

Chilwell wasn't going to let the shout from his London rival get to him after what was a dream start back in England.



He left Strasbourg on Deadline Day to join Palace for a second time and scored the Eagles' winner after fellow left-back Tyrick Mitchell scored two before being substituted.

"To be fair, T [Tyrick Mitchell] had scored two from left wing-back," he said. "So it must have been a day for the left wing-backs.

"We spoke about the past few days, when I've been interviewed, but I'm buzzing to be back among the boys.

"I love being here, so to come back and score the winner in front of the Palace fans, it was great to see how buzzing the boys were.



"It's a great feeling."

Sports.title: Michael Carrick 'bitterly disappointed' as Man United are held to draw at Everton with last-minute wonder goal - and admits leaky defence must sharpen up
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick admitted that Manchester United’s draw at Everton felt more like a defeat after Ainsley Maitland-Niles fired a dramatic equaliser in the final minute of injury time.

Benjamin Sesko looked to have given United victory at the Hill Dickinson Stadium for the second season in a row when he struck in the 88th minute, but Maitland-Niles celebrated a dream debut by making it 2-2 at the end of a week in which he joined Everton on deadline day.

‘We’re bitterly disappointed,’ said Carrick. ‘It feels like a defeat. It's a bit of a cliche, but we have taken a point and we can't ignore that, but it feels like we should have had a lot more.

‘All the work that went into putting us in that position, to then come away like that leaves us with not a great feeling.’

Bryan Mbeumo fired United in front right after half-time before Tyrique George levelled with an excellent strike, and Maitland-Niles produced an even better one to cancel out Sesko’s header.

United have conceded two goals in all three of their games so far this season against Hull City, Ipswich and now Everton, taking a total of four points.

Ainsley Maitland-Niles lets fly with a stunner to earn a point for Everton in the dying moments

‘We haven't started the season that badly,’ Carrick insisted. ‘We've got that close to coming away with three points today. There are moments we can deal with a bit better, but we'll be fine.

‘Obviously we can't ignore it. We need to concede less goals to give us a better chance of winning games. We'll certainly look at that and keep improving.

‘There's obviously things we need to get better at as a team. There's been two strikes from distance really, two really good strikes from their point of view. Sometimes they fly in the top corner and more often than not they probably don't.’

Marcus Rashford was one of United’s brighter players but had to come off in the second half after appearing to hold his hamstring moments earlier.

‘He was just feeling a bit of something,’ Carrick confirmed. ‘He looked really sharp and dangerous again, but that final moment didn't quite drop for him.’

While Carrick was left feeling as though he had lost the game, it was quite the opposite for Everton after Maitland-Niles struck five days after completing a £4.2million move from Lyon 45 minutes before the deadline.

Maitland-Niles was delighted with his wonder strike and praised the home fans

‘It felt like a win,’ said the former Arsenal player. ‘It's amazing. Everyone wants to start off like that and thankfully I did. The ball fell to me on the edge of the box, I put my foot through it and it ended up in the top corner which I'm happy about.

‘We dug deep and managed to get a point. The crowd were with us and we were fighting to the end and that's why you get those results.’

Everton boss David Moyes paid tribute to his new signing, saying: ‘We are still getting to know Ainsley. If nobody knew you, that goal would get your plenty of headlines. It was a brilliant goal.

‘United played better than in other games. I didn’t think we deserved to be behind, but we lost the first goal a minute into the second half which was shabby. Then we allowed them to go 2-1 up, but it would be hard to say we didn’t deserve anything.’

Sports.title: Jamie Vardy returns to England! Striker and wife Rebekah to move back from Italy as he signs surprise deal at Burnley - who are rock bottom of the Championship
Sports.content:
Jamie Vardy will be playing his football in England again after signing a contract at Burnley until the end of the season. The 39-year-old has been a free agent since leaving Italian side Cremonese in the summer following their relegation to Serie B. Vardy, who moved to Italy with his wife Rebekah and their family, scored seven goals and provided three assists in 29 appearances in Serie A last season. Burnley will be hoping Vardy's experience can help them improve after a poor start to the season – with the Clarets bottom of the Championship after five matches. They want him to be their No1 striker and his deal has an option for a further year if Burnley are promoted. It is understood he turned down offers from MLS, Serie A and the Premier League. The scale of his task is clear with the club yet to win a game in the English second tier so far this season – drawing two and losing three of their matches, scoring six and conceding 12 across those matches. Upon signing for the club, Vardy – who had a Netflix documentary about his career in May – expressed his desire to propel them back up the table. Jamie Vardy is back in English football after signing a deal at Burnley until end of this season The move sees Vardy and his wife Rebekah return to England after he played a year in Italy He scored seven goals and provided three assists in 29 Serie A games for Cremonese He told the club's website: 'I'm really happy to now be here at Burnley. 'This club has a proper footballing history and passionate fans who deserve a team that represents them and their town. 'I can't wait to get going on the pitch and help the team move in the right direction.' Burnley head coach Nicky Hayen is excited about what his new striker will add to his struggling squad. He said: 'We are delighted to welcome Jamie to Burnley. 'His experience and leadership will be invaluable to our squad, and we believe he can make a significant impact on our campaign. Jamie has a proven track record, and we are looking forward to seeing him in a Claret shirt.' Vardy scored 200 goals in 500 matches for Leicester and won both the Premier League and FA Cup with the club. He is regarded as one of the club's greatest players of all time. The striker also scored seven goals in 26 appearances for England and was part of the Three Lions squad for Euro 2016 and the 2018 World Cup.
