Sports.title: The 6/10 man who looks like he's still finding his way, the recurrent menace - and the star who never got to grips with his opponent all game: Everton 2-2 Man United PLAYER RATINGS
Sports.content:
The 6/10 man who looks like he's still finding his way, the recurrent menace - and the star who never got to grips with his opponent all game: Everton 2-2 Man United PLAYER RATINGS

Manchester United were stunned in the final seconds as Ainsley Maitland-Niles scored his first Everton goal in stunning fashion to rescue a point for David Moyes' side.

United looked to have nicked the victory in front of the away end when Benjamin Sesko headed in late on.

But there was a final twist in the tale and roared on by a buoyant South Stand, former Arsenal defender Maitland-Niles let rip from distance to leave United goalkeeper Senne Lammens stranded as he watched it fly into the top corner.

It was a strange old game, one first ignited by Bryan Mbeumo, who fired United ahead less than 60 seconds into the second half, and then flipped on its head when Tyrique George lashed in his own stunner to open his account for Everton to level it at 1-1.

Sesko, on from the bench, responded from there before Maitland-Niles scored a stunner to send the Hill Dickinson Stadium into raptures.

Daily Mail Sport's NATHAN SALT was in position in the Hill Dickinson Stadium to cast his eye over both teams...

Ainsley Maitland-Niles was Everton's hero as his last-gasp strike rescued a precious point

There was only seconds left when the former Arsenal defender let rip from outside the area

EVERTON (4-2-3-1)

Jordan Pickford – 5.5

So often he has proven himself to be Superman but even he can’t keep opponents out forever if Everton are offering so little at the other end. That being said, a goalkeeper of his experience cannot misjudge a header like Benjamin Sesko’s that badly. Knew as soon as it went in he’d cost his side.

Merlin Rohl – 5

First, the good. Rohl put in the cross of the game in the first half to tee up Barry, only for his team-mate to fluff the header while unmarked in the area. Now, the bad. The issue was that he became unplayable at the other end as Marcus Rashford ran past him with ease. Was hooked – wisely- soon after getting booked.

James Tarkowski – 6

Made a goal-saving tackle on Matheus Cunha from about two yards out at 1-0 down to at least give Everton hope of a comeback. Lost his bearings to allow Sesko a free header in the box, which is unforgivable. Ultimately, it’s going to be a long season for the likes of Tarkowski if those ahead of him don’t pull their finger out. Feels like a sitting duck.

Jarrad Branthwaite – 6

Didn’t do much wrong at the back or much right in attack. A fairly non-descript afternoon for a defender that spent years on United’s radar. Given his size, Everton need to find a way to make him more of a weapon on set pieces.

Vitaliy Mykolenko – 4

Not good enough. Too slow off the mark as Mbeumo drove forward to score and then enraged 90 per cent of this stadium when he hesitated to go for a 50-50 with Cunha when United looked to break following a corner. Makes the wrong decision time after time after time.

Vitali Mykolenko too often makes the wrong decision and United exposed that time and again

James Garner – 6

The former United academy midfielder started well, fizzing balls around and he was quicker to loose balls, much to the annoyance of Michael Carrick. But his influence waned as it wore on and he eventually left with cramp.

Harrison Armstrong – 6.5

Fans love him and there were moments here to see why they were so vocal in expressing their desire to keep him from the clutches of Nottingham Forest. Often found himself exasperated at the lack of support, and lack of ideas, around him. Booked for a stray arm clipping Bruno Fernandes.

Brennan Johnson – 5

Everton was supposed to be a reset for a player that has never kicked on since scoring the winner in the Europa League final, ironically against Manchester United, in Bilbao. Johnson has plenty of experience but didn’t come close to truly troubling United’s back-line.

Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall – 5.5

The focus of Everton’s latest viral supporter chant but certainly not the focal point of this side, despite playing as the No 10. Drifted through too much of this game. Needs to demand the ball, put his foot on it and manufacture some attacks, just like Jack Grealish did when he came on. Take more responsibility.

Tyrique George – 8

The Everton youngster had Diogo Dalot seeing stars for much of the afternoon as he spun him inside and out before producing an absolute thunderbolt to open his account for the Toffees. Everton’s attack looks porous after a nightmare transfer window but George is a diamond. Keeping him fit is essential.

Tyrique George was a constant thorn in the side of Manchester United and deserved his goal

Thierno Barry – 6

Should score 43 minutes in when Rohl’s cross goes over the head of Maguire to give him a free header a handful of yards out. Two stunning strikes helped Everton to a point here but if they are to kick on this season they simply have to have Barry – the only senior centre forward on the books – fit and firing.

MANAGER: David Moyes – 7.5

Has his hands tied after the mishandling from those above in the transfer window but credit to him for his substitutions here. Jack Grealish changed the game and Ainsley Maitland-Niles produced a famous goal that won’t be forgotten here. Fortunate, but you make your own luck in this league.

SUBS

Jack Grealish (for Brennan Johnson, 66) - 8

Hayden Hackney (for Merlin Rohl 75) – 6

Ainsley Maitland-Niles (for James Garner, 77) – 7

MANCHESTER UNITED (4-2-3-1)

Senne Lammens – 6

Was on a watching brief for much of this until Everton unleashed two missiles in his direction that no goalkeeper in this league is keeping out. Sometimes you have to hold your hands up and accept it as a goalkeeper and here were two prime examples. One of those days.

Diogo Dalot – 5

Never got to grips with Tyrique George all afternoon and has to find a way to adapt his game when he knows the winger has him for pace. Picked up a late booking as he became frustrated, which wasn’t a surprise given so little came off for him.

Harry Maguire – 6

Looked like his race may have been run when he was flattened inside two minutes after a nasty clash of heads with Barry. Got away with one when Barry misguided a header after he’d peeled off Maguire but all in all the towering centre back was perfectly fine.

Harry Maguire was dejected as he looked up while on his knees after Everton's late equaliser

Lisandro Martinez – 6

A quiet game from the Argentine and that’s not always the worst thing. Made a couple of key headers but his through-the-lines passing, something which massively elevates United to being a top team, was largely absent here. When there is only one striker to deal with – and not a great one – he needs to do a lot more with the ball.

Luke Shaw – 8

So much pressure is on Shaw’s shoulders to stay fit and go the distance after United elected against signing another left back. On this evidence he’s bang up for the challenge. Immense at both ends and his cross was on the money for Sesko to nod in. Ran up and down and showed no signs of fatigue.

Youri Tielemans – 6

Still feels like he’s trying to find his way in this side and find the best way to influence games as he so often did for Aston Villa. Does the basics really well and some of his footwork is as delicate as a ballet dancer.

Kobbie Mainoo – 6.5

Didn’t have the influence that he showed in the demolition of Ipswich Town last week but he always showed for the ball, even after being caught in possession a couple of times early on. The next stage of his development will be finding that next gear to dominate and dictate games like this.

Bryan Mbeumo – 7

Has a habit of struggling for long spells in games but keeps adding goals and this was a beauty to break the deadlock. Mbeumo is not a natural winger and did look more suited in Ruben Amorim’s 3-4-2-1. But what he is good at, when his confidence is up, is putting the ball in the net. Needs to keep being direct up against inferior full-backs.

Bryan Mbeumo set United on their way but he needs to stay direct when beating his man

Bruno Fernandes – 6

Let his team-mates have it when he found himself committing to the high press and others didn’t follow suit. Hit the crossbar eight minutes in after connecting to Mbeumo’s header and was a busy bee chasing after the ball. Second half his control on proceedings waned and United needed him to calm it down when it became a back-and-forth contest.

Marcus Rashford – 7.5

Go ahead and hit the ‘like a new signing’ klaxon. Rashford was a complete menace down the left and had the beating of Rohl all afternoon. Deserved an assist for his deft backheel inside the area which had the goal at Cunha’s mercy, save for Tarkowski’s heroic interception. Performance wise, United’s best player for the 70 minutes he was on the pitch.

Matheus Cunha – 6

So often shows moments of real quality but in equal measure he can be just as frustrating when his execution is off. Being deployed through the middle doesn’t maximise his game but three touches in the Everton area and just one wayward shot to his name before coming off, you expect more.

MANAGER: Michael Carrick – 6.5

If his sides cannot go on to kill games, like they did last week when Ipswich lost their heads, then they will always be susceptible to suckerpunches like this one. Looked absolutely gutted at the end after the Sesko substitution paid dividends with the 88th-minute header. That’s back-to-back away games without a win now.

SUBS

Patrick Dorgu (for Marcus Rashford, 70) - 6

Benjamin Sesko (for Matheus Cunha, 70) – 7

Leny Yoro (for Diogo Dalot, 84) - 6

Andrey Santos (for Kobbie Mainoo, 84) - 6

Sports.title: George Russell's title hopes in tatters as Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli wins Italian Grand Prix to extend his championship lead - despite starting 19th
Sports.content:
Kimi Antonelli came from 19th on the grid to win the Italian Grand Prix, all but ending the title hopes of George Russell, who started second and finished second.

In triumphing on a strategy that favoured him rather than his Mercedes team-mate Russell, Antonelli, aged 20, became the first Italian to win his home race since the black-and-white days of Ludovico Scarfiotti in 1966.

A pivotal moment came on lap 28, when Lance Stroll’s Aston Martin broke down. A virtual safety car was deployed. Antonelli was called in, offered the chance for a cheap stop to move from hard tyres to mediums.

He came out flying but 14 seconds behind race leader Russell, who had stayed out and was thus handed the task of making his harder rubber last to the end with an ever-diminishing advantage.

At times, the to-be-winner Antonelli lapped nearly a second quicker than Russell and it was a matter of whether he would close the deficit to the Briton by the 53rd and concluding lap.

It set up a grandstand finish. With 10 laps remaining, the 20-year-old was 4.7sec back. It looked bleak for Russell. It was going to come down to the last nervous moments. Or not quite as long as that, in fact.

Kimi Antonelli roared to victory in his home Grand Prix, becoming the first Italian to win it since 1966

George Russell, starting second and finishing second, could only congratulate his team-mate

He was told: ‘Let’s take no risks. Let’s bring it home.’

Antonelli arrived on Russell’s gearbox on lap 49. They skirmished at the first corner. All fair. Russell went deep. Antonelli ran into the gravel. Russell kept the lead. But a lap later Antonelli did what was now increasingly looking like the inevitable at Variante Ascari. He took the lead, and that was that.

His Mercedes was fast but it was also a brilliant drive, albeit helped by having a strategy that was most useful to him.

An early shunt brought about by Charles Leclerc’s huge shunt on lap two got him on to hard tyres under the red-flag opportunity. Russell moved from mediums to hards. He was not helped by this, though, arguably he should have been far enough up the road by some stage never to have been under threat. He had, after all, started 17 places ahead of Antonelli.

The Mercedes garage hailed the win as you would expect – unbridled emotion. Antonelli is their favoured son. Russell, who finished 3.8sec back from him, is not. He is also 66 points back from Antonelli and has no momentum.

It is almost impossible to see a way back for him.

Max Verstappen, for the record, finished third. Lando Norris was fourth and Oscar Piastri fifth. Lewis Hamilton was sixth for Ferrari.

It was a yo-yoing race, a good show in some ways but one that revealed not only the strengths but frailties of the new regulations introduced this year which allow one car to pass with a boost and then be repassed as their electric charge falls off.

Early on the race was suspended following Charles Leclerc's 160mph smash into the barriers

Leclerc was left devastated on the grass after crashing out of the race

You don’t need to chuck it down the inside and provide a moment you will remember. It was silly at times, but will have played well with audiences that seek instant gratification.

Early, Leclerc was left sitting in pain after his dramatic 160mph crash.

The Ferrari favourite lost control of his car at the final bend, the Parabolica, as he duelled with Piastri for fourth place.

Leclerc’s impact with the wall was severe with only a short portion of gravel to slow his trajectory into the hoardings, which he thudded side-on.

The Monegasque soon jumped out of the car but then sat disconsolately on the grass as he was comforted by a marshal before being taken away in the medical car. He was feeling his neck as he went for treatment. Ferrari said he had been released from the medical feeling ‘OK’.

The race was red-flagged for 30 minutes and some fans in the grandstands cried at the huge blow for their team.

By this point, Leclerc had already squeezed Hamilton on the second part of the opening chicane and was driving somewhat erratically. Hamilton was furious, saying: ‘Charles pushed me off.’ The seven-time world champion, who started fourth, fell down to 10th place.

Russell was leading the race for Mercedes at this point when the race was suspended after passing pole man Pierre Gasly, who was to finish seventh for Alpine, on the main straight at the end of the first lap.

Leclerc’s stricken car was taken away by crane and the ding-donging began again.

Sports.title: The potential of Michael Carrick's Man United is in danger of being buried under bad habits - their lack of killer instinct was exposed in Everton draw and their results so far should serve as a warning, writes IAN LADYMAN
Sports.content:
The potential of Michael Carrick's Man United is in danger of being buried under bad habits - their lack of killer instinct was exposed in Everton draw and their results so far should serve as a warning, writes IAN LADYMAN

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Amid all the disappointment and rancour of Everton's transfer window, Ainsley Maitland-Niles slipped in the back door almost unnoticed. As the club tried and catastrophically failed to sign a centre forward, the recruitment of a defensively-minded utility player was never likely to turn the dial very much.

Indeed in his own programme notes for this game, Everton manager David Moyes said only of the 29-year-old that 'we are looking forward to getting to know him'. Suffice to say, that job is now done.

Here by the Mersey, in a stadium slowly preparing itself for another shot of stomach turning disappointment, Maitland-Niles - once of Arsenal but recently of Lyon - eased on to a loose ball in the final seconds of the 95th minute and thumped in a goal from 25 yards to rescue a point for his team.

What a goal. What an ending. What a story. Only the sixth league goal of Maitland-Niles' career, it was one of the best this fabulous stadium has witnessed in its short lifetime. For Everton, it earned a point that - after a dismal first half - they ultimately deserved. For United, it served to remind us once again that the very best we can say about Michael Carrick's team is they remain a work in progress.

Comfortably superior in the first 45 minutes, United seemed to have won the game twice. Once when Bryan Mbeumo scored beautifully in the first minute of the second half and again when substitute Benjamin Sesko headed them back in front at the end of normal time and six minutes after Tyrique George's own spectacular effort had levelled for a resurgent Everton.

Ultimately, Carrick - wearing a rueful look as he walked off at the end - will wonder when he is going to see a 90-minute performance from his team. Everton improved markedly once they fell behind for the first time and the Hill-Dickinson crowd became engaged. But Carrick will wish to know just how his team lost momentum almost as soon as they went ahead. It took George's equaliser 37 minutes later for them to wake up again.

Ainsley Maitland-Niles rescued a point for Everton on debut against Manchester United

Maitland-Niles equalised in second-half stoppage-time with this stunning long-range strike

The frustration was etched on United boss Michael Carrick's face at full-time after their draw

It all carried something of an England-Argentina vibe and for Carrick it represents a problem. This season will be a darned sight harder than the last one. It will test his squad in every way. This week, for example, United must play in the Champions League on Thursday before hosting Manchester City three days later. Ouch.

Carrick will need his team to show more resolve than this. He will need to see a greater killer instinct. He will need to see his captain Bruno Fernandes jumping to his feet when tickled by James Tarkowski rather than lying down as though sniper shot.

At the moment the good stuff - and there is a fair amount of it - is in danger of being buried beneath bad habits. After three games - two against promoted clubs - United are in the bottom half and that should serve as warning if nothing else.

With the Everton fans bouncing and singing at the end, memories of the first half had disappeared in a haze of adrenaline and excitement.

The opening period had ended with Everton defender Jarrod Branthwaite sliding in to make a tackle on the breaking Marcus Rashford and then jumping up to block Fernandes' shot on the follow-up.

With the crowd rising to acclaim him, Branthwaite responded with a gesture suggesting that maybe he and his team-mates could do with a little more of that.

Branthwaite maybe had a point. Up until that point, this had been a very peaceful afternoon down by the Mersey. A day perhaps to yearn for the some of the atmosphere they had left behind at Goodison Park.

Equally, crowds need something to feed off. They need something with which they can engage and their team had given them precious little. It was as though the anti-climax of the transfer window had cast a spell on everybody.

Bryan Mbuemo (left) roars with delight after scoring the opening goal for Manchester United

United - without actually scoring - had revelled in it. They had played the game at their pace and were left largely untroubled as they did so. The home crowd yearned for a strong challenge or a thumping header or a piece of individual skill. None of it came and, as such, Branthwaite's double intervention right at the end of first half stoppage time felt like a moment.

United should have been ahead by that point. They had created space and width and opportunity but had not managed to find the right final pass, the right decision or indeed the right finish.

Carrick stuck fast to the formula employed in the 5-2 beating of Ipswich last Sunday. Rashford was in on the left side and was progressive until feeling his hamstring in the second half and Kobbie Mainoo retained his place in the centre of midfield ahead of summer signing Andrey Santos.

Everton are down on numbers. Jack Grealish - back again on loan from City - was on the bench at least and young Harrison Armstrong was in the team after his club decided against selling him to Nottingham Forest after threats of a supporter revolt.

Moyes' team for too long looked limited in more ways than just bodies. They were often short of early ideas, too. Here, they didn't lay a glove on United until striker Thierno Barry headed over from a Merlin Rohl cross in the 43rd minute and Branthwaite drove a shot low at Senne Lammens moments later.

MATCH FACTS AND PLAYER RATINGS Everton (4-2-3-1): Pickford 5.5; Rohl 5 (Hackney 75, 6), Tarkowski 6, Branthwaite 6, Mykolenko 4; Garner 6 (Maitland-Niles 77, 7), Armstrong 6.5; Johnson 5 (Grealish 66, 7.5), Dewsbury-Hall 5.5, George 7.5; Barry 6 Goals: George (83), Maitland-Niles (90+6) Booked: Armstrong, Johnson, Rohl Manager: David Moyes – 7.5 Manchester United (4-2-3-1): Lammens 6; Dalot 5 (Yoro 84, 6), Maguire 6, Martinez 6, Shaw 8 (Mazraoui 90+1); Tielemans 6, Mainoo 6.5 (Santos 84, 5); Mbeumo 7, Fernandes 6.5, Rashford 7.5 (Dorgu 70, 6); Cunha 6 (Sesko 70, 7) Goals: Mbeumo (46), Sesko (88) Booked: Shaw, Maguire, Dalot Manager: Michael Carrick – 6.5 Referee: Mr John Brooks - 7

Prior to that, it had been all United. Carrick's team still look a little unbalanced without a proper centre forward - Matheus Cunha did the job here - but they attacked with menace and speed and the return of Rashford down the left side has certainly helped with that.

Fernandes was first to threaten with a hooked volley on to the bar in the eighth minute. That started with a Luke Shaw cross from the left and that side of the pitch was a problem for Everton all afternoon.

Another cross, this time from Rashford in the 22nd minute, created another issue for them and Cunha should have done more than side foot over from 18 yards after Diogo Dalot stepped over the ball to give his team mate the chance of the half.

At times, it looked a little too easy for United. There was no edge to the game at this stage. Everton had their best spell just before the break but within a minute of the game restarting, their opponents were in the lead.

Mbeumo had been hitherto quiet but when his dart infield from the right touchline saw a gap appear, he ran between Vitali Mykolenko and George to curl a superb low shot across Jordan Pickford in to the far corner. It was a quality goal from a very good player and United had the goal their superiority had deserved.

Everton now had a choice. They could either wither and die or find some kind of gumption with which to respond. Happily it was the latter and from this point on the game changed in a way that tells us much about the psychology of football.

As United drew their heads back in to their shells and with it lost all of their authority, Everton grew on the back of naked need and twice could have equalised before the hour as Barry and Brennan Johnson were in turn denied by blocks from Lisandro Martinez and Shaw.

The second one was quite spectacular from a player many United fans had hoped would have been replaced in the summer. But at least we now had a game and an atmosphere and the feeling of renewed energy was only heightened when Grealish emerged from the bench with 25 minutes left.

The loanee from City had been featured on the front of the match day programme with Everton hoping he could find some of the form he showed here last season before injury struck him down.

By now the pattern of the game had fundamentally changed. Everton's desperation had added the necessary bite to their football and as a result United started to look a little rattled.

Fernandes annoyed everybody bar his own team-mates and his own away support by staying down after that feather touch from Tarkowski before Dalot was booked for hauling back Grealish.

With the game now being played almost exclusively in the United half, Everton just needed a moment of quality to bring them that they were starting to deserve. In the 83rd minute it arrived.

Everton equalised through Tyrique George's thunderous effort to make it 1-1 on 83 minutes

United looked to have won it late on when Benjamin Sesko headed home, but it wasn't to be

Hayden Hackney - a genuinely clever summer signing from Middlesbrough - made inroads laterally and was given a second chance when his misplaced pass came back to him off Martinez. This time he found George down the right and a rising shot from Everton's best outfield player crashed past Lammens and high into the net at the near post.

United perhaps were partly to blame. Their efforts to find a second goal had been limited to say the least but at least they responded. This is a United squad with a little more depth to it and when Shaw crossed from the left in the 88th minute substitute Benjamin Sesko headed down and in when Pickford probably should have saved.

Everton have seen this script before. So have United. But just when it seemed Carrick's players were set to leave the field talking about character and resolve and spirit, they were cut down at the death.

Maitland-Niles - an Arsenal trainee from the age of six and subsequently of Ipswich, West Brom, Roma and Southampton - can expect more than a line in the match programme next time round.

Sports.title: Tiger Woods makes first public appearance since five-year driving ban... as loyalties with Kai Trump torn after Vanessa's public show
Sports.content:
Tiger Woods makes first public appearance since five-year driving ban... as loyalties with Kai Trump torn after Vanessa's public show

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Tiger Woods was spotted all smiles on the sidelines at Stanford Stadium on Friday night, making his first public appearance after being hit with a five-year driving ban.

The 15-time major champion returned to his alma mater for the Cardinal's college football clash against the Miami Hurricanes, days after his courtroom appearance.

Sporting a white Stanford cap and a wool quarter zip from his own brand 'Sun Day Red,' Woods was seen laughing and chatting with staffers on the sidelines.

He appeared relaxed and upbeat as he soaked in the action and was also seen in conversation with West Coast rap icon E-40 before the action got underway.

However, the matchup presented an awkward clash of loyalties for the golf legend.

While Woods remains one of Stanford's most celebrated alumni – having won 11 collegiate tournaments before turning pro – his personal ties now run deep in Miami, given his relationship with Vanessa Trump.

Tiger Woods was spotted on the sidelines at Stanford Stadium on Friday night

The 15-time major champion returned to his alma mater for the Cardinal's college football clash

It marked his first public appearance after being hit with a five-year driving ban

Vanessa's 19-year-old daughter, Kai Trump, recently moved to South Florida to begin her freshman year as a collegiate golfer for the University of Miami.

The granddaughter of Donald Trump has regularly documented her move on social media, sharing snaps in Hurricanes gear as she begins her collegiate golf career.

On Friday night, it was Kai's new school that walked away with all the bragging rights, as Miami blew out Woods' beloved Stanford Cardinal in a 45-6 rout.

The outing marked a stark change of scenery from Wednesday morning, when Woods appeared alongside Vanessa to resolve his criminal case stemming from a March 27 crash near his Jupiter Island estate.

Woods' girlfriend held hands with him at the Martin County Courthouse in a show of public solidarity as he finalized his plea deal over a March rollover crash.

Woods pleaded no contest to a reduced charge of reckless driving and refusal to submit to testing, avoiding jail time after entering a plea agreement.

As part of the deal, Woods will have his license suspended for five years.

President Trump declared Woods's plea deal 'very fair' as he weighed in on the matter, just one day after the golf legend discovered his fate from the ordeal.

He added: 'But I think he's going to have somebody drive him. I told him that a long time ago: 'Why don't you get somebody to drive you'

'So he's going to have somebody drive him from now on. He's just a very special guy and I'm glad that was resolved.'

Trump added: 'It's a very tough situation because they didn't find alcohol on him. You know, he didn't test positive at all for alcohol. It's a tough deal when you're taking a painkiller because you're under pain... and you have a problem and you test positive.'

The 15-time major champion was found at the scene of the crash in Jupiter, Florida, with two opioid tablets in his pocket, on March 27.

He has since spent time in rehab in Switzerland but had not been seen publicly since arriving back in America until last month.

According to police, Woods was driving at a high speed along a beachside road when his Land Rover clipped a tractor-trailer truck and rolled onto its side, causing about $5,000 worth of damage to the other vehicle.

Sports.title: Middlesbrough fuming as Burnley's Turf Moor pitch destroys their white kit by staining it GREEN... and the truth behind the BBC's failure to land Commonwealth Games - INSIDE SPORT
Sports.content:
Middlesbrough fuming as Burnley's Turf Moor pitch destroys their white kit by staining it GREEN... and the truth behind the BBC's failure to land Commonwealth Games - INSIDE SPORT

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Middlesbrough were left furious after their trip to Burnley for their Championship clash saw their team’s kit destroyed.

Kitmen at the Teesside outfit were staggered to see green stains all over their previously pristine white shirts and shorts following the final whistle of the 1-1 draw at Turf Moor last week and club officials quickly sought an explanation.

It transpired that the culprit was a chemical put down by the Lancashire side to treat a nematode, or roundworm, problem on the playing surface, which contained a pigment which turned the visitors’ all-white outfit green.

An industrial stain remover failed to do the trick when the visitors returned home, with flabbergasted Boro officials making the incident known to the EFL and now thought to be considering a request for compensation.

Such was the extent of the damage that boots and even goalkeeper gloves were impacted. ‘I’ve never seen anything like it,’ explained one insider.

Burnley’s next opponents at Turf Moor? Derby County…

Aidan Morris celebrates Boro's 23rd minute goal in a pristine white kit... which appears to have been stained a shade of green by the time he applauds fans off at the end of the 1-1 draw

Revealed: BBC didn't even make offer to televise dramatic Commonwealths

Contrary to reports last week that BBC Sport offered a paltry £900,000 to televise this summer's Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games, Inside Sport understands the corporation failed to table any kind of official monetary offer for the 74-nation multi-sport event that saw Scotland's Josh Kerr win the Commonwealth Mile, English sprint sensation Amy Hunt run 100m in under 11 seconds and Wales' Emma Finucane pick up four golds in the velodrome.

The revelation may add to the pressure on under-fire BBC Director of Sport Alex Kay-Jelski, who has presided over a series of changes that have proved unpopular with some. There was no daily World Cup preview show and Football Focus and Ski Sunday have been axed, while the use of content creators has drawn criticism.

Inside Sport also understands there has been some internal dismay at a decision not to send any reporters from BBC Sport’s website to European away matches featuring English clubs this week.

With the BBC safely out of the picture, TNT Sport acquired the Glasgow 2026 UK television rights via a significant financial bid.

The Warner Bros Discovery sports channel and their streaming platform HBO Max then broadcast more than 600 hours of live coverage – three times what the BBC broadcast from Birmingham 2022.Other parts of the BBC showed up their TV decision.

Amy Hunt landed 100m silver at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow

Radio 5 Live took UK radio rights alongside talkSPORT, and there was extensive coverage across BBC online and social platforms, including TikTok, aimed squarely at the younger audiences the corporation says it is desperate to reach.

An estimated 100 BBC personnel were accredited for Glasgow 2026, despite British audiences having no live free-to-air TV option. BBC Sport's apparent short-sightedness was confirmed when millions tuned in for the European Athletics Championships weeks later.

And Glasgow offered far more than the track, including Duncan Scott, Adam Ramsay-Peaty and Tom Dean in the pool and Britain's best cyclists in the Sir Chris Hoy velodrome, with para events fully integrated into proceedings. All faced stiffer opposition than a European field, with Australia, Jamaica, Canada, South Africa and Nigeria among the 74 nations.

The centenary edition of the Commonwealth Games in India is four years away. It remains to be seen if the BBC will atone for what many are viewing as a clear error.

League One keen to join promotion expansion

League One could be set to follow the Championship’s lead by expanding the play-offs to include another two clubs.

Currently those finishing in third to sixth place contest the end-of-season showdown for a spot in the second tier. However, to increase interest and opportunity, officials now want to follow the Championship’s lead and extend that by two teams, giving those who finish in eighth place a shot at promotion.

League One representatives on the EFL board have put forward the proposal, with a decision expected in due course.

Olympiakos fans not happy with Forest...

Colourful Nottingham Forest owner Evangelos Marinakis may have a problem on his hands in his native Greece.

A quick look online shows Olympiakos supporters are increasingly angry at what they see as their club becoming a stepping stone for their owner’s Forest project.

Olympiakos paid a Greek-record €16million (£13.75m) to sign Colombian midfielder Gustavo Puerta from Racing Santander on deadline day, with the 23-year-old initially tipped to sign for Forest before moving to Olympiakos on loan.

Evangelos Marinakis has owned Olympiakos since 2010 and Forest since 2017

Colombian media now report that Puerta has been told he will spend one year in Greece before swapping Athens for the bright lights of the Premier League and Forest.

Having already seen four players move from Forest to Olympiakos this summer, that has tipped many fans over the edge, with one claiming Marinakis is ‘diminishing Olympiakos’ and another demanding the club be ‘free from these ownership groups and this nonsense’.

The discontent comes as Olympiakos’ fortunes have changed drastically since Forest’s promotion – they won 22 Greek titles in 26 years before Forest returned to the Premier League in 2022, but have triumphed just once in the four seasons since.

Sports.title: Jack Grealish makes 'nightmare' claim after completing Man City exit
Sports.content:
Jack Grealish makes 'nightmare' claim after completing Man City exit

Jack Grealish has reunited with David Moyes after heading to Everton for a second straight season as the Manchester City outcast seeks to resurrect his career

View 2 Images Jack Grealish has talked up his relationship with David Moyes

Jack Grealish has confessed that David Moyes will probably see him as "a nightmare" after his second return to Everton on loan.

‌



The playmaker spent last season at the Toffees and had proved influential in the final third until injury curtailed his season. The Manchester City star headed back to the Etihad in the summer, but it quickly became apparent that he was set for a peripheral role.

‌



Grealish had been gradually cast aside by Pep Guardiola, who once spent £100million to sign him, and even after the Catalan left City and Enzo Maresca was hired the 30-year-old was set to remain on the outer.

‌



Everton returned to land him for a second time ahead of his contract expiring next summer and it will leave Moyes again looking to get the most from Grealish. The England international admits the pair have a great relationship - and that helps get the best out of him.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Speaking to Sky Sports he said on the Everton boss: "I get on really well with him. He’d probably tell you, sometimes he’d probably say: ‘Jack’s a nightmare,’ but we have this really good connection.

‌



"And like I was saying to you off camera, when I get on really well with a manager, it makes you want to do more for them. It makes you want to give everything for them, play well and succeed for them. And that’s what I want to do. I know a lot of the players are like that with him here.

"When I look back to managers that I’ve played my best football under, I always had a special connection with them as well. Three of my managers, Tim Sherwood, Steve Bruce and Dean Smith, I always speak to all of them now on text. I played such good football under all of them and I feel like that with the manager here as well."

View 2 Images Jack Grealish's days at Man City could be over (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Last season Grealish scored twice for Everton and was of interest to several clubs, including former side Aston Villa and Sunderland, before opting for a return to Merseyside.

Moyes and the Toffees endured a hectic end to their summer - winger Iliman Ndiaye made a £65m switch to City but Everton failed to add the striker they'd be eyeing despite being close to a £40m deal for Monaco and USA forward Folarin Balogun. They also failed with a bid to re-sign Brazil striker Richarlison from Tottenham.

Grealish came off the bench and had an impact as Everton came from behind to draw 2-2 with Manchester United on Sunday.

Sports.title: Gary Neville and Ian Wright disagree over six Premier League stars - 'Not having that'
Sports.content:
Gary Neville and Ian Wright disagree over six Premier League stars - 'Not having that'

Arsenal face Chelsea in Saturday's Premier League blockbuster at the Emirates Stadium as both teams look to protect their perfect starts to the season

View 2 Images Gary Neville, Jamie Carragher, Daniel Sturridge and Ian Wright (Image: Sky Sports)

Gary Neville and Ian Wright got into a disagreement about the quality of the forward lines in the Arsenal and Chelsea squads. The sides go head-to-head in the Premier League on Sunday afternoon, where both the Gunners and the Blues have a 100 percent record on the line.

‌



Arsenal defeated Coventry City and Aston Villa in their first two Premier League matches of the season, while Chelsea earned wins over Fulham and Brighton.

‌



Wright and Neville were part of Sky Sports’ punditry team for their coverage of Arsenal vs Chelsea at the Emirates Stadium, and the duo got into a debate about the forward options available to Xabi Alonso and Mikel Arteta.

‌



Neville suggested that he believes Arteta would prefer Chelsea's attacking resources over the players currently at his disposal at Arsenal.

Xabi Alonso confirms Chelsea star's position switch before Arsenal showdown READ MORE :

"If you say to Mikel Arteta: 'Would you swap your forward line for Chelsea's?' He would swap," Neville said.

"He'd put [Morgan] Rogers, Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro up there in front of [Bukayo] Saka, [Kai] Havertz and [Ebere] Eze, he would. So it's not the strongest part of Arsenal's team, but what he's done in defence and in midfield has become that good.

‌



"If you don't concede goals, you've got a great chance of winning nearly every single match. If you're conceding goals, you're going to lose more points."

Wright, however, took exception to Neville's view, with the Arsenal icon responding: "I'm not having that over Saka, Havertz and Eze. I'm not having that."

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



View 2 Images Arsenal and Chelsea go head-to-head on Sunday afternoon

Neville then responded by saying: "You don't think he'd [Arteta] pick Rogers, Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro over those three [Havertz, Saka and Eze], Ian?"

Wright replied: "Not for me, no." Neville then concluded the debate by saying: "Oh dear."

‌



Arsenal strengthened their attacking options this summer by bringing in Christos Tzolis, though they sanctioned the exits of Leandro Trossard, Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus.

Chelsea, meanwhile, have also strengthened their forward line considerably, with Rogers being joined by Geovany Quenda, Danny Welbeck, Emmanuel Emegha and Dastan Satpaev in making the move to Stamford Bridge before week's deadline.

Sports.title: F1 Italian GP suspended after huge Charles Leclerc crash and Lewis Hamilton battle
Sports.content:
F1 Italian GP suspended after huge Charles Leclerc crash and Lewis Hamilton battle

The Italian Grand Prix was brought to a halt after Charles Leclerc crashed into the tyre wall at Monza

View 2 Images Charles Leclerc crashed into the tyre wall on the second lap of the Italian Grand Prix. (Image: Sky Sports)

The Italian Grand Prix was red-flagged just two laps into the iconic Monza race after Charles Leclerc suffered a major crash. The Monegasque driver collided with the tyre wall on the second lap after losing control of his Ferrari at the tail end of the Parabolica.

‌



The 28-year-old was able to exit the car and appeared to be winded as he walked away from the wreckage. The rear end of the Ferrari got away from Leclerc as he attempted to correct the slide, but he couldn't keep the car on the track, skidding off the gravel and hitting the wall at some speed - with a force later revealed to be at 60G.

‌



The race was brought to a halt soon after, with red flags out on track, to allow the safety team to recover Leclerc's car from the gravel trap and make repairs to the tyre wall.

‌



Lewis Hamilton risks Charles Leclerc wrath with request to Ferrari bosses READ MORE :

F1 star stripped of podium 48 hours before Italian GP in double penalty as FIA announce ruling READ MORE :

It was an awful start for Ferrari in their home Grand Prix with both of the Prancing Horse drivers battling it out in the early stages of the race.

Lewis Hamilton dropped to P10 and claimed he was pushed off the track by Leclerc on the team radio, with his title hopes drifting away. The incident was noted by the FIA, but it's unlikely anything will come of it, given Leclerc's crash.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



Hamilton is expected to restart the race in P8 after regaining some positions, but Ferrari were dealt a huge blow when Leclerc crashed, having been battling for P2 against Pierre Gasly.

The Alpine driver started the race in a shock first pole position of his career, but Gasly was caught by George Russell's Mercedes down the straight at the end of the first lap.

View 2 Images Charles Leclerc suffered a major crash at the Italian Grand Prix

‌



Championship leader Kimi Antonelli began from the rear of the grid following an engine penalty, but the teenage sensation had worked his way up to P12.

The restart came from a standing start with Russell on pole and Gasly alongside him on the second row. Franco Colapinto moved up to P4 after getting past Piastri in the wake of Leclerc's crash, but before the red flag was deployed.

It's been a disappointing couple of weeks for the Ferrari duo, with Hamilton frustrated that Leclerc didn't let him pass in their last race outing at Zandvoort, despite being the faster of the two cars.

Article continues below

Leclerc's crash means that Ferrari need a strong end to the race from Hamilton with only one of their cars left out on the track.

Sports.title: Unai Emery makes telling Alejandro Garnacho comment as ex-Man Utd star slumps to new low
Sports.content:
Unai Emery makes telling Alejandro Garnacho comment as ex-Man Utd star slumps to new low

Alejandro Garnacho has endured a very difficult few seasons and his loan spell with Aston Villa appears to have got off to a tricky start following his switch from Chelsea

View 2 Images Garnacho is set to spend the season on loan with Aston Villa (Image: Getty Images)

Aston Villa boss Unai Emery believes Alejandro Garnacho still needs time to adapt having played just half an hour for the club. The Argentine forward joined Villa on loan this summer from Chelsea.

‌



There is an obligation to make that move permanent at the end of this season should certain conditions be met. But Garnacho’s contributions in the Midlands have been limited so far.

‌



He has made just three substitute appearances for Villa so far this season, while he has also fallen behind academy graduate George Hemmings in the pecking order. Asked how he has managed to earn that position, Emery has suggested that the youngster is already a Premier League player, while Garnacho still has work to do.

‌



Speaking after his side’s 0-0 draw with Hull City on Saturday, Emery said: “George, he worked last year the whole year with us and played minutes. He is performing fantastic and getting better.

“He created one assist for Buendia. He is working in the intensity and kilometres we need. He is doing it. I think he is a player now, clearly, to be in the Premier League.

‌



“Then, we have other players who joined who need to adapt to us in training, playing matches, and Garnacho is in this way.

“We need their performance to try to add things, working and getting numbers. Garnacho is in this way. How he is responding, George, is really fantastic.”

Garnacho’s move to Villa follows a very tricky couple of years for him. He fell out of favour at Manchester United, ahead of a switch to Chelsea.

‌



View 2 Images Garnacho has yet to start for Aston Villa this season (Image: Getty Images)

But he lasted just a year at Stamford Bridge, scoring just once in 24 Premier League appearances. He underlined his desire to rediscover his confidence during his time with Aston Villa.

"This is an important club which is going up really quickly, so I can't wait to get started here," Garnacho said after his switch to Villa was announced. "I was looking for a club to get my confidence back, so I can try to become the player I was a few years ago in my first years at Manchester United.

Article continues below

"I spoke with the manager and he gave me the confidence to try to help the team here - that's why I'm here. It is important to play in European competitions and the Champions League is the best one, so the fact we are playing in it this season makes me really happy. Hopefully we can do something important in it."

Sports.title: Arsenal missed out on two transfer targets 'due to Andrea Berta's approach'
Sports.content:
Arsenal missed out on two transfer targets 'due to Andrea Berta's approach'

Arsenal spent heavily in the summer transfer window as they attempt to reclaim the Premier League title but a number of deals did not come off for the Gunners despite Andrea Berta’s best efforts

View 2 Images Andrea Berta's attempts to sign Page and Monga ended in frustration (Image: Getty Images)

Arsenal reportedly missed out on a double deal for Leicester wonderkid’s Jeremy Monga and Louis Page due to Andrea Berta’s unconventional negotiation tactic. The Gunners were linked with the pair as part of a recruitment drive that has seen them hoover up a number of the country’s most promising youngsters.

‌



They have already signed Igor Tyjon from Blackburn Rovers, Manchester United’s James Scanlon as well as Cardiff City starlet Axel Donczew. The North London side have also agreed a deal to sign Georgian youngster Andria Bartishvili.

‌



Arsenal were keen to add Monga and Page to that list, the pair having made a huge impression in the East Midlands but summer switches did not come to fruition. According to BBC Sport, Arsenal’s sporting director Andrea Berta chose to conduct negotiations with intermediaries as opposed to with Leicester colleagues, which is not an unusual move for him, having done the same with the move for Bruno Guimaraes.

‌



But a lack of club-to-club contact on this occasion was cited as a reason as to why moves were not completed. Instead, Monga chose to switch to Premier League rivals Manchester City for £12m, while he has subsequently joined Championship side Swansea City on a season-long loan.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Page in the meantime ended up staying with Leicester despite late interest from Manchester United. Despite that, Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta remains satisfied with a window that has seen the side spend close to £200m.

‌



Asked if he was relieved if the window was closed, the Spanish coach replied: “It is what it is - we don’t decide! I think we all know we had to make a decision on when we wanted the window to be closed, and now that’s it, and now it’s crystal clear everybody’s squads and where everybody has to be."

On if there was any deals that got away, he said: “I don’t know - I think every moment, every situation is different. Sometimes we need to react because something unexpected happens as well, and you need to be prepared for that, so I think every case is different.”

View 2 Images Arsenal were interested in both Louis Page and Jeremy Monga (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Arteta added: “I don't know, these are just opinions. The window is closed and I prefer to look at all the incredible things that we have in this squad and not to spend any more time on the things that are not part of us right now. That's it and that's my main responsibility.

“Yeah, 100% ticked. The outcome after can be different to what you expect, but the intention is certainly there, which is, in my opinion, what I value the most.”

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso confirms Chelsea star's position switch before Arsenal showdown
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso confirms Chelsea star's position switch before Arsenal showdown

Xabi Alonso is still deciding on his best XI at Chelsea but he is certain that captain Reece James has a long future in central midfield, rather than at right-back

View 2 Images Xabi Alonso is all-in on Reece James in midfield (Image: Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC via Getty Images)

Xabi Alonso has backed Reece James to become world-class in central midfield, hinting that his future lies away from right-back for Chelsea.

‌



Alonso is not the first manager to field James in the middle of the park. Having played the vast majority of his career as a right-back, the Chelsea captain has started in midfield for club and country over the past year.

‌



Having sold Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City for £125million on deadline day and failed to bring in Lamine Camara as a replacement from Monaco, Chelsea are shorter in midfield options. Moises Caicedo, Valentin Barco, Jordan Henderson and Romeo Lavia are the specialist options, but Alonso has taken a different approach this season.

‌



Chelsea have been using a 3-4-3 formation since Alonso arrived as manager this season and the Spaniard has used both James and Malo Gusto in central positions. Speaking ahead of their trip to north London to play Arsenal on Sunday, Alonso hailed James' potential in the position.

FOLLOW OUR CHELSEA FB PAGE! Latest Blues news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Asked if James could become a world-class right-back, Alonso replied: "I would say so. He is very comfortable and confident playing in that position.

"He has the intelligence to play there because, in the middle, you need to be able to connect with your team-mates and know what the best thing to do is before you get the ball.

"He has this awareness. I remember him playing very, very well playing in the middle. So we are using him and he will have a lot of minutes as a midfielder."

‌



He added: "For me, physically, when he is fresh and prepared, he has shown he can compete in the Premier League – no issue. As a midfielder, you have to take a lot of easy decisions and many right decisions. You are very connected to the game and are close to the action. Walking is not possible.

View 2 Images Reece James can play in midfield or at right-back for Chelsea (Image: Vince Mignott/Getty Images)

"So Reece is very involved in the game and knows where he needs to be. He has the capacity to help the team-mates around him and that is very important to me because he has this presence where he has respect from his teammates. When he says something, they listen and they follow him."

‌



James was left out of the starting XI for the 4-3 win over Brighton last weekend, with Gusto playing alongside Lavia in the middle of the pitch. The failure to land Camara in a £47m deal from Monaco on deadline day was a disappointment, but Alonso is sure they have enough quality in the position.

“We have this feeling with the squad that we are good to go. If we have these setbacks in the season with injuries and suspensions, we have this feeling that we will be able to manage," he said.

“Time will tell, but at the moment he (James) is having a very important role in that position. I knew [before I joined] that he could play there.”

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
